reviews.review:
Prior to coming, thankfully I had made a reservation on resy because the place (huge space) was fully seated by the time we arrived at our reserved time! Also upon entering, there is a narrow walkway leading into a huge, high ceiling dining space! We got 2 pitchers of drinks to start- the orange ginger and passion fruit! I personally liked the passion fruit over the ginger because it was sweeter and had a floral scent to it! What's a night of soju drinking without some jeon(pancakes)!! We love a good kimchi jeon! It was crispy and light with a nice kick from the kimchi! 
Moving onwards to the BBQ, we were looking forward to trying the wagyu trio, but sadly they were all out! Our server suggested the kkot deung shim and it did not disappoint! This was a dry aged, grass fed rib eye and our server cooked it well (leaving a slight pink in the center)! We also got some tangsuyuk and carbonara to share and to end the night, we had some coconut gelato. 
We ended up staying pretty late and moved over to their bar for some more drinks and it was a nice cozy area with booths for groups. Overall, it was a great night of good food with good drinks!

We were looking for a spot to try in Brooklyn and noticed this place after seeing it get two stars in a New York Times food review. The atmosphere has a charming, old-school feel with wide wooden tables that give off a rustic, vintage vibe, almost as if you've stepped into a classic steakhouse from a different era. The warmth of the wood really adds to the cozy, inviting ambiance.

The steak was cooked to perfection, and we loved that we didn't have to grill it ourselves, which made the experience even better. The service was excellent, and the drinks were delicious. The steamed dumplings were a nice surprise--yummy and perfectly prepared. Overall, it was a great spot that lived up to the hype!

I've only visited the bar, three times within the last three months, and each time I've ordered the wings in both flavors. Pretty standard wings and satisfies my cravings. Friendly and attentive bartenders. Solid cocktail list and draft beers with local selections. It's in my regular bar rotation. 

The karaoke rooms are fun and reasonably priced. Experienced it for birthday parties. Wide selection of songs to choose from.

Very disappointing!! We asked about the quantity of the galbi bbq and our waiter said it would feed two to three people, so because we were only two people we ordered it. 

The quantity that arrived was comical and would probably feed one person. Two to three... bffr. 

We left hungry and really disappointed. The food was fine but definitely not good enough to justify the price point and small portions. The rice was subpar and the banchan was not good at all. I understand being more experimental outside of the traditional banchan that Korean restaurants serve but it just wasn't good.. 

The kimchi also tasted really mediocre and flavorless  - like something cheap from a grocery store. 

It's a nice looking restaurant but don't waste your time here. We had to leave and get more food elsewhere since we didn't leave satisfied.

the ambiance and vibe is nice, but this place is overpriced and disappointing and i would not recommend it. save your money for elsewhere. 

my friend and i were considering the bibambap (~$22) that we had once before and it was pretty good - but wanted to try the bbq. we asked the server how much the galbi ($50) would serve and he said between 2-3 people. it was probably enough food for 1.2 people. 

we should have known something was off when they served us the smallest plates of the most mid banchan and BAD KIMCHI. it was giving white woman "healthy" version of korean food. the rice was brown rice (we didn't ask for) and poorly cooked. 

overall the galbi tasted fine but it was barely any food and we left hungry. won't be going back - i recommend you go to threes brewery next door for dinner instead.
This place is amazing,  the staff is super nice and the ambience was great! The food was also delicious!!

this review is for karaoke. it was a saturday evening. the mics were weak. i couldn't really hear the singers through the speakers. you cannot adjust pitch. it's done through healsonic app. there was a disco ball in it, but no bright light shining on it. the couches were nice and if you are already eating at insa, it's a nice thing to do afterwards, but it wasn't great as a standalone karaoke room. usually a line for the bathroom.  there were nine of us, we booked for two hours. We are not a big drinking group so ordered exactly one carafe of house saki and one pitcher of beer. the bill was $640.00. the bill was high because I accidentally booked a room for a larger group (180 per hour= 360) but then there was a "karaoke fee?", etc? It wasn't a big drinking group so the total was a complete surprise. this is a quiet-ish out of the way area of brooklyn!

The food tastes as if it was refried and reheated - it was not fresh or tasty.  The service is poor, and the restaurant ambiance overall feels stale and uninviting.  It's expensive for no reason at all.  You can find better food elsewhere for cheaper.  A disappointment event for a birthday dinner.

This review is for the bar. Its a nice and cozy spot to have a few drinks with friends. Liked that they had a wide variety of korean drinks and cocktails, and comfortable booths to sit at. The bar tenders were friendly and place was clean.

The restaurant section is spacious and welcoming, and they even have karaoke rooms. Would come back next time to try the food/karaoke.

I would come here for the appetizers alone. My friends and I ordered the dumplings, pork buns, broccoli, wings, and seafood pancake. We enjoyed all of them, but that Broccoli is the best I have ever had. We ended up ordering it twice. The kimchi fried rice is good and spicy. The short rib is a must have. It was flavorful and was cooked to our liking.  As for the drinks, you only need one. They definitely do not skim on the alcohol. Come here for a chill time with friends.

The ambience was inviting and welcoming by host, servers and staff. Decor and style was tasteful and layout of bar and dining area gave a party atmosphere with privacy in the bar dining room! The food was deliscious and tasty with Gochuchang and spices in the tofu and seafood soup! The bulgogi and fried broccoli was very good and noodles were excellent! I recommend this restaurant for great Korean American experience!

I'm Korean and this is legit while also being more comfortable than traditional korean restaurants.  We sat in the bar and shared broccoli, dumplings soondubu, bibimbap. I had Drifting Moon cocktails. It was delicious . The panchan is a little sweet for my taste but otherwise fine. Service was great.

this is for the karaoke experience and the karaoke experience only. i booked a reservation here for the a karaoke room with 7 people for my bf's bday and here are the pros and cons of my experience

pros 
- prompt service: they have a button which you can press for service and they were very responsive and brought our orders quickly! 
- good selection of music: they got most all the songs up til like late 2021/2022
- rooms: the room wasn't big but it was clean and the seats were arranged in a way that we could all see each other! 

cons
- they tried to keep our cake: i brought a cake to be cut (they have a cake fee btw) and they took it to the kitchen, brought it out half way thru our reservation with candles, took it back to slice and bring it out - all of which was great. EXCEPT they gave us the tiny slices, which FINE but then despite asking twice where the rest of the cake was, was ignored and then had to flag down the hostess as we were leaving to ask her to give us the rest of the cake. there was over half left! they tried to swipe that ish and that really rubbed me the wrong way
- bad speaker: i don't know if it was just our room but we kept getting this loud popping sound and despite flagging it twice, it did not get fixed. they did knock off like $30-50(?) off the final bill but it did ruin a lot of the songs we were singing
- app/remote: you do have to download an app to access the songs which is convenient once you set it up but i wish their remote service was better so you werent just passing around someone's phone

overall, i'd come back here if i'm looking for karaoke in the area but definitely wouldn't go out of my way to come back especially when there are SO many other options in the city.

Insa is a super fun place and great for birthdays, especially if you want a dinner that transitions into an activity later in the night that doesn't require moving a group to another location. Just beware that a private karaoke room is pretty expensive and you will probably need a reservation.

i've eaten here four times in the past year and i am blown away by the dishes every single time. The service is sharp, the ambiance with the BBQ tables is fun, and the cocktails are perfect, but it's the food that keeps me coming back. 

As someone who is gluten free but loves korean food, you just can't beat this. There's also great BBQ options for vegetarians and vegans- im not veg but even I love the fresh grilled mushrooms! 

This place is a true gem in the brooklyn food scene, do not sleep on it
Was excited to try this restaurant.  Unfortunately Korean food in brooklyn is disappearing. This place included.

Fantastic top to bottom. can't wait to go back. The Corn Gratin was definitely a highlight but the pork belly, mushrooms, and ribeye were wonderful. Great vibes in the space plus karaoke in the back were a plus. Our server Kris was fantastic as well, he knew how to be attentive and weigh in in all the right ways. I'll be back!
Sat at the bar and had a very pleasant meal. The bartender was very good. The bar room had a cozy ambiance. I had the corn and the stuffed zucchini. Delicious.

Very disappointing dinner for a hefty price point

My friends and I came for a dinner for three at Insa on a Thursday evening. The restaurant was very pleasant and had a more of an opened layout which was nice. 

We ordered some KBBQ - Galbi, Mushroom Platter and the Pork Belly. In addition, we got some appetizers - the fried mushrooms and spicy pork ribs. Out of all of the food, the spicy pork ribs were the most memorable and everything else was simply disappointing. 

The server was cooking the entire time at the table, and when I say the entire time, I meant the entire time. They were flipping the meat the whole time until it was done and off the grill. It was very awkward because usually they step away and come back to check. The portion size of the meats were also very small... there was only 6 thin pork belly slices (more like bacon strips) for $32. The mushroom platter which had no flavor whatsoever, $30. The Galbi which was $48 was also small in portion size. 

We all left feeling hungry because there was simply not much to eat from each plate. I would not recommend this place from the portion size to the price to the flavor. It's not worth it...

Ambiance - good open space
Food - meh. Fried squid was very salty, meat was okay seasoned
Service - it was painful watching the server handle the meat .. the grill plate was burned and she still add meat on top instead of changing the plate

Will definitely not go back

Disrespectful servers who do not like Korean food and say so explicitly to customers. This sentiment is evident in preparation and service. Do not order jajang - zero understanding of the dish at Insa and the beautiful first date culture behind the sauce. When Insa opened it was a beacon for bringing authentic Korean food to Brooklyn, founded on the beautiful food and service at Good Fork, but has now become a clown show of bastardization of servers who tell customers they dislike Korean food and treat ingredients with disgust. Recommendation: close this place down if you care about Korean culture.

Honestly, pretty disappointing. The biggest thing that I have to say is that 4 out of 7 of the things we ordered came out wrong or were forgotten because the servers don't know the names of the dishes when ordered in Korean...at a Korean restaurant. We never saw our server again after we corrected the order for the 3rd time and nothing was taken off of the check. Too bad because the ambiance is cute and chill!!

Mid-ass kimchee. A deadly insult. But the bartender made a special ask to deliver it to me after I expressed astonishment when they said the kitchen is closed at 1030. I don't think the owner(s) will care.

No hite or OB available?

The bill came out and $23 became $50 somehow? I had to follow up in some interminable fashion to get this right. 

Sketchy vibes.

Don't walk. Run. It's amazing. I'd move in if I could. 

Get a bbq table if you can and watch the magic happen. The waiters kindly help you cook the food (I'd be lost without Fernando), and it's always delicious. 

My favs are actually not from bbq though - the japchae (glass noodles made of sweet potatoes) and ooommgggg the bulgogi. Do it do it do it. 

One of my top spots for kbbq in Brooklyn.

Let's start off by saying that the only positive thing about this experience, giving it the 2 stars, was the customer service. Employees were very engaging and polite. 

Now... Let's get into it. 

This was an utter disgrace to the Korean culture. The food was not Korean in the slightest -- maybe the kimchi side dish, which was probably store bought, yet still very dry. 

The galbi cost a whopping $48 per serving and was a poor cut of steak that could've probably cost $7. 

Unfortunately, the best bite of the entire meal was the skin of the steamed dumplings. 

All I have left to say is that if all food tasted like this, I'd be the skinniest person ever. I wouldn't wish this food on the roaches of the city.

I had so much fun here. The food was delicious, service was excellent. Karaoke was fun. Beautiful and comfortable inside. The food is all served family style, great for a party. Highly recommend the cauliflower and the chicken wings.

I've never been to a bar where they shame you for drinking. I pay my tab and always tip but still consistently get an attitude for drinking. Not sure what they strive for -  a group that drinks seltzer? yes the drinks are great and there aren't many karaoke options in Brooklyn but the shaming has to end. if you don't want people drinking become a music library. I'd love to come and just listen to your tunes while I sip seltzer.

I've had a bunch of things on the menu the few times I've been here and the only thing I LOVE is their japchae. It's consistently great and a huge portion. But everything else I've had has been not so wonderful. (Though I did try their lemon mochi cake last week and it was delish.) 

Cute space, karaoke is fun, but I'll mainly be coming back for the japchae.

Got here late like 9:40 (because they close at 10) but me & my date was so hungry after a long day there wasn't anything else open in the area. Thankfully we were seated & served well, love the ambiance/aura of this place plus the food was delicious. I will definitely go back, at an earlier time of course lol

Fun atmosphere with long tables, not very private. Had the panjeon, salad, and kalbi. The real star was the dessert - like a mochiko cake with berry reduction and a nice little scoop of vanilla ice cream. 

Fun to watch the chef cook the kalbi in front of us, but she had no conversation to share with us.

I has such a great experience here. 

I tried a whole bunch of things on the menu, starting with the candied sardines and the ban chan. 

The sardines are such a fun flavorful snack and I wish I could have a bag of them to snack on while watching tv. I loved all of the banchan especially the pickled pear. The tangy potato salad was also an interesting twist. I'm not a huge kimchi person but the plain kimchi here was so delicious I couldn't stop eating it. 

I also got the tteokbokki which had a really pleasant texture and a decent amount of heat, as well as the dumplings and the fried mushrooms. The deep fried mushrooms was probably my favorite item I tried. The flavor is subtle but delicious and the lemon honey sweetness cut the richness of the deep fat fried mushrooms well. The dumplings were ok, I loved the deep fried crispy exterior which reminded me of a fried wonton.

I also had the kimchi budae which was predictably fantastic because their kimchi is just so balanced and delicious. 

The interior of this restaurant is so cute and comfy. If you're not getting bbq you can sit in the bar area which has big soft booths and such a nice atmosphere. I stayed here for way longer than I normally would have and kept eating more food just because it felt so cozy and pleasant to sit there and chat.

I went here because I originally wanted to go to Mokbar but I didn't realize they aren't doing dine in right now so I just went to another Korean restaurant closest by, but I definitely will be returning because everything about my experience here was amazing.

Not particularly great Korean food,some things are okay and some just not acceptable (wilted browned lettuce for Ssam, jesus). but the kicker is the really awful service.  The waitress was indifferent at best, but mainly non existent or completely dismissive (one entree we had to ask about twice before it came after most of us were finished).  In any case, mediocre, expensive Korean with crappy  service doesn't lend itself to recommend.  Had I seen the mixed low reviews before would definitely have skipped it, poor reviews fully confirmed.  Skip it.
If you come here, I highly suggest you also stay for karaoke in the back! Come with a larger group and enjoy delicious food then drunkenly sing together in one of Insa's karaoke rooms.

This was my first Korean BBQ experience. We went there as a group of 4 and we had the Galbi, which was super juicy and melt in your mouth. We also ordered the pork, but once you've had the Galbi you really can't enjoy anything else...IT WAS THAT GOOD!! I sent my friends there the week after!

RAW Fried Chicken. We ordered fried chicken for a main course but it was RAW when we bit into it . We sent it back and didn't want another. The attitude was "Yeah, okay, whatever"- NO apology, no acknowledgement they wrecked our dinner, just an attitude when we asked that be taken off the bill. I'm hoping I won't get food poisoning from what I did eat . And we were quiet about it too.  To add further insult to injury. The banchan cost $5 and was minuscule and lame. If you want Korean (that won't give you food poisoning) go to 32nd street. PS- I just saw a revues from 9 MONTHS AGO with the same raw chicken problem, and apparently, the restaurant does not give a damn.

Closed Mondays & Tuesdays

Really nice place to celebrate a birthday. We came here with a group of 8 and got a karaoke room for two hours. Someone walked us into the room and explained all the rules even though only half the group had arrived. You can download an app to control which songs to put on next if you do not want to flip through the book they have there. You must ask for the wifi password before you can download the app. The man who kept coming in to refill our water and take empty plates out was very attentive. I had no problem with the service during the karaoke portion of the night. 

We got a passion fruit soju bowl (8/10- probably would not get this again), melona cocktail, high noons (which come in orders of 4, 8,10) , and fried mandu. Both the vegetable and meat mandu were good. I actually preferred the vegetable mandu more. The sauce it came with was also very good. At times, the bathroom like got long because there are only 2 bathrooms. 

We walked past the very cozy bar section and had to leave for an hour because the barbecue section was so fully booked. (There's a cute brewery across the street) Fast forward, one hour later, we were seated at our table. Everything is very open. One thing that surprised me was they only had ginger ale.

For dinner, we got pajeon, which is a pancake with garlic  and chives. Everyone enjoyed this and we eventually ordered a second one. For BBQ, we got galbi, pork belly, shrimp, and an order of mushroom. Surprisingly, the mushroom order came with a variety of mushrooms and was my favorite thing that night. Our waitress came by the table to see if we wanted anything before the kitchen closed. I also appreciated her telling us to be careful when she was switching the hot BBQ plates. The banchan was "bottomless", but if was hard to get a refill. 

We got a brownie sundae for my friend's birthday and it smelled very good. It was served in a hot plate to warm the brownie, so the wax actually melted too. We wanted to surprise my friend, but the waitress came by and asked if we wanted any desserts besides the surprise cake. 

Overall, it was a good place to celebrate a birthday, the food was good, but some things could be improved upon.

Everything was delicious- the bar was a great place to start. Highly suggest making a reservation.
The meats are cooked for you here.

I tried Korean bbq for the first time ever here and I really enjoyed my experience. The wait was long but very worth it. Everything we ordered was so tasty. This included the steamed vegetable dumplings, scallion pancakes, and the marinated beef short rib which was cooked to perfection by our server. Our server was so kind and guided me throughout the whole process. He really took care of us and I'm grateful. I do wish they had more selections of wine but the bottle we got for the table did just fine. We finished with the mochi cake which was just the right amount of sweet. I would definitely come again.
Loved it. Walked in and waited for a table at the bar, which is so cute I love the decor. Everything I tried was soooo good. So worth waiting for

One of the top 5 or so restaurants in Brooklyn, and the best Korean. Delivery or in house are both phenomenal. Best dishes are the rice cakes, the udon noodles with the gochujang and squid, the fried chicken, and anything off the bbq. When we get delivery, i always get an extra 1/2 pint of their gochujang to cook with. At $5, it is a ridiculous value, better than anything you can get at most grocery stores for a lower price.

I used to love this spot as a regular, but the experience has gone downhill. I especially did not appreciate my server's snarky attitude tonight -- I have food allergies and it's always been graciously accommodated here. When I gave my server the allergens I need to avoid, she made several sarcastic comments "oh the chef is going to love you" etc and would not stop fixating on it, as if her goal was to make me feel awkward and uncomfortable about it. Past servers have always told me it's not a problem and made no big deal about it. She was bad vibes and her rudeness ruined the entire experience, ugh. I'm also Korean, so to have a white woman give me a hard time in a Korean restaurant was extra irritating and problematic. Cocktails and quality and authenticity of food also used to be a lot better in the past. It was good while it lasted, but I'm never coming back! (just go to k-town; better food and staff)
its not cheap but the quality is very high. Dine in experiences have been lovely, cocktails are particularly delicious. Delivery has always been reliable too. I'm very fond of the dried anchovies.

I'm really disappointed in my last experience at Insa but not for a reason I'd have ever expected. I went for a friend's birthday dinner. We ordered a ton of food and a fair number of cocktails. Service and food were great.  While we were still eating our dinner, we were suddenly asked to move to the bar area to finish our meal because another reservation was coming in and they needed the table. We had been there about 1 hour and 45 min, but we had just ordered another round of drinks at that point and hadn't finished our mains or ordered dessert. That said, there were several other tables that had arrived there before us and were still seated and were not being asked to move. I was pretty offended by the request, but I politely asked the waiter to figure out another solution because we were celebrating a birthday and were't ready to give up the table. Important to note -we were eating at a normal pace (in line with how quickly we were served) and were not just squatting so we could chit chat. They allowed us to stay in our seats until we finished our dessert, but as we did, I watched the restaurant practically empty out. No one was coming for our table. I have no reason to believe it was actually needed. My suspicion is that we were asked to move because we were a table of 40 somethings and everyone else in the restaurant was younger. I can't imagine what other reason there would be other than that one - but I hope I'm wrong. For the rest of the meal, it was on my mind and I felt like we should be rushing to leave. In any case, it sort of tainted the whole experience which would otherwise have been good.

food is not traditional Korean ... service was poor . Ordered the Jjajang shrimp and assured it was black bean sauce... tasted like sweet and sour shrimp  ...noodles ?? Served Lukewarm .  All for fusion and different twists on traditional food but definitely not my taste nor Korean tasting  . Expensive for what was served .

Was quite excited to find a Korean BBQ in Brooklyn at first and don't have to travel to Manhattan, photos looked great, space was well designed and spacious. 
Now on to the food - it is way over priced for what you are getting, the side dishes are tiny, small portion. You have to keep asking for lettuce and they'd bring you 3 pieces at a time.
Service was ok- staff are nice but not really trained to cook the food like what you'd expect from a typical Korean bbq, our server would not stop turning the meat as if they don't know it's done or not, only a few pieces was cooked right and there aren't many to begin with.

If you are looking for a traditional Korean bbq, this is not the place.

Good quality food for sure and a romantic setting.But very small portions for a high price. Not cool at all. How is it I go to have dinner and still leave hungry ? Then, another 80 dollars for Karaoke ?? Also the wait time for each order is 30 minutes, it's hard to get someone's attention for help and we weren't greeted with water until we had ordered food. I was parched ! When collecting everyone's portion for the bill, we asked for change for a big bill and the waiter just assumed the remaining change was his tip. We waited for 20 min for the damn change. Unbelievable ! I do not see myself coming back !

For Korean barbecue, this is the place to go in central Brooklyn. Literally everything on the menu is delicious. The fried chicken was incredible, the squid salad was so tasty, the NY strip was divine and we had multiple helpings of the cucumber salad - it was that good! Dumplings were showstoppers. The Thai iced tea ice cream is out of this world - tastes more like Thai iced tea than Thai iced tea tastes like Thai iced tea! Oh, and the soju ... spectacular! Get every flavor!

This place is very unorganized, rude and disrespectful. Before I went to the restaurant I called and I asked if I could make a reservation and the guy upfront said he couldn't put me in  and that I can come to the restaurant and he would let me in. After I got to the restaurant the wanted me wait 2 hours .

Went here for my friends birthday and it was the perfect celebratory spot! Shout out Josie our server, she was the best and grilled that short rib to perfection! Y'all gotta order the short rib. The seafood scallion pancakes were also a must. Beyond the food, this place as a wonderful array of drinks that are all delicious. And, there are several private karaoke rooms in the back that are great fun, especially if you're a bit drunk! The staff is so nice and loving and let us sing our hearts out. One of my favorite korean BBQ experiences!
The service was absolutely terrible. We received a table and we barely had someone taking care of. I do not recommend this place even though the food is good.
Very good, great service, good drinks. We did karaoke after dinner, which was very convenient since the restaurant has both dining and karaoke.

Went for the first time (summer 2021), ordered seafood pancake, bibimbap, jja hang noodles. First let me say this to folks that want "real Korean food" for cheap - don't expect Insa to be a place where you get loads of freebies and big portions and what you think is "classic" junky salty pre-made sauce Korean food. 

My family used to own a small korean restaurant and I know that it takes loads and loads of work to create different types of banchan that are normally offered for free!! And except for kimchi, they don't keep, so you have to remake it daily if you care about quality. Our entire family worked long hours to prep, chop squeeze mix roast toss fry marinade all sorts of banchan and couldn't put that into the price of the main dishes bc everyone expected them for free. Terrible $$ sink. Wish we charged but it wasn't a sensible thing to do 15 yrs ago. 

Today Korean cuisine where it's no longer a cheap eat (usually implemented through cheap labor) and means ingredients and labor are being more fairly paid for. You SHOULD pay MINIMUM $5 for banchan to cover for ingredients and labor, not to mention service and rent. Youd easily pay $5 for latte or a bowl of lettuce "salad" that takes zero effort. I MEAN JACKS WIFE FREDA CHARGES $15 FOR A SINGLE WAFFLE with two berries on top and it's loved. But paying $5 for banchan is injustice? Change your standards please or go somewhere else. 

On service, I think they're responding to that. They were very friendly the entire time and we were super impressed. I hope they keep it up. That's a key part of the guest experience. 

Vibe is nice, we stayed in the red bar room which was great for little kids as it was quieter during the earlier dinner hours. 

Flavor was great. Thought that the seafood pancake batter was a bit too fluffy, and the bibimbap could have used some more beef, but overall felt like a clean taste. The cabbage kimchi could use some more fermentation and anchovy sauce for some kick. It did taste like it was made by someone who doesn't actually eat kimchi. 

One set back was that there was a piece of steel wool in the noodles, which we reported to the kitchen. The chef apologized and put the entire meal on the house. I get that this can happen, but that's pretty dangerous with kids in case of accidental ingestion. I would suggest they review their wipe down practices. For this they get 3* otherwise it would have been 4*.

I've been here several times over the course of several years and this place has really yanked in the past two years. Very disappointed and ashamed at what Insa has become. 

I wonder if Sohui Kim is aware of how the food has dipped in authenticity to the point where I can't taste the difference between the food from Insa versus buying the food at H-mart instead. I think I can buy better pre-prepared/frozen food from any Asian supermarket than what was prepared for me today. Maybe the food can pass for some uncultured fans of this place, but I've been able to access enough authentic Korean restaurants in this city to know I'm getting completely overcharged for something and it's just disgusting to me. 

In addition, the service was so dismal that the wait staff was clearly overworked and not even greeting the tables properly or cracking a single forced smile during service. +Didn't want to help bbq our meat. + Ran out of water at our table with no refills. + One of the bathrooms didn't flush. ‍

What a shame. The idea and intent was a good one, just executed horrifically and worsened over time.

This place is an embarrassing attempt at Korean food. They managed to fail in every aspect of the spectrum: service, portions, and quality of food. The owners spent all their money on the interior design and ran out of money to hire competent chefs and waiters.

Service:
The waiters looked like they were forced to work there without pay. Our water pitchers were constantly empty and we had to ask for them to be refilled every time. They have no incentive to treat their customers well since there is a mandatory 20% tip on the bill.

Portions:
The portions here are SMALL. My 5 year old niece could come here and would leave starving. We had 12 people and had to do the prefix menu. We chose the pork belly and galbi as our BBQ options. After the first plate came (which doesn't even feed ONE person), they turned off the fire which confused us because we literally had 1 piece of meat each. We had to ask the manager if there was more coming and ONLY then they brought out another plate which equated to a whopping 2 pieces per person. These guys are literally committing robbery of $75 per person.

Quality:
Dumplings and squid salad were okay. Fried chicken was the worst Korean fried chicken I've ever had. It tasted like they bought the Korean BBQ red marinade from Hmart, smothered the chicken and fried it. Also it was way too salty and SO DRY. Best of all, one of our guests bit into a piece that wasn't fully cooked. The pork belly and galbi were less than mediocre.

This place is absolute trash. Go to the worst Korean spot in k-town or flushing and you will have MUCH better food spending 60% less money.

We came here with a party of 12 and had their selected pre fixed menu. Now let me start with their portion amount, 2 orders of galbi, 2 orders of pork belly. Every person had about 3 pieces of galbi and 3 pieces of pork belly. They even forgot to bring lettuce for the pork belly. Now that bbq is out of the way, let's get into the starters. The banchans, there were 3 sets of banchans, enough for ants, but they forgot we are human beings. After the banchans, they brought out 3 plates of mandus, consisting of 8 mandus per plate, so about 2 mandus per person. If we were all on weight loss diets, it would have been enough. Next came 2 orders of fried chicken, most of it was dry and salty, some were undercooked. How do you even achieve overcooked chicken and undercooked chicken at the same time... very interesting cooking techniques for sure. After the chicken, came 3 orders of squid salad, which was decent and 3 orders of japchae, which was mediocre. Lastly they brought out 4 hot fudge sundae, now there's clearly 6 couples in this party. How do they expect us to split 4 sundaes with 6 couples? 3 people per sundae? All boys on one side and girls on the other? I don't know. 

Now with the extremely mediocre food out of the way, let's crunch some numbers.
Prefixed menu was $75 per person. 12 people total was $900 dollars. Let's take a look at their menu a la carte https://www.insabrooklyn.com/menus
You can look it up online, the pricing as of this review will be stated below.

2 orders of Galbi $42 each = $84
2 orders of pork belly $30 each = $60
3 sets of banchans $5 each = $15 which Korean bbq place charge for banchans?..... anyway moving on
3 orders of gogi mandu $15 each = $45
2 orders of fried chicken $39 each = $78
3 orders of squid salad $17 each = $51
3 orders of japchae $20 each = $60
4 orders of hot fudge sundae $12 each = $48

For a total of $441 if we order a la carte. Now, if the food was bad, it's our fault for picking the restaurant. But if you're going to blindly rip us off, that's bad business practice. They charged us over double of what we should've paid. For what? For taking their prefixed menu? I mean if the prefixed menu was marked up 20-30% we will be fine. But it's marked up over 104%. Now that's daylight robbery.

If you want to get ripped off for some extremely mediocre kbbq. This is the place to go!
I mean you can reasonably expect to either get quantity or quality when going out to eat. This spot did not hit either one of those

We did the prefix for $75 per person. No one was full at all. Fried chicken was super salty and undercooked. The grilled meat portion of the prefix was so small, everyone only got a bite each. The meat they gave for a party of 12 is literally one small plate of short rib that you can get at any other kbbq spot for $30 and a small plate of thin pork belly usually $25. Quality and flavor compared to other kbbq spot is not better either to justify the price. They brought out one other serving of short rib and pork belly after someone in the party asked if that was all for the grilled meat.

The pictures i posted look 10x better then the actual food. 

Chicken was either dry or raw in center, squid salad was ok, the jap chae was probably the beat dish.
I got so disappointed and disgusted i didnt even bother taking pictures of the pork belly(flavorless) or the galbi(states marinated, but flavor is missing ‍)

Came for a group dinner with a prefix menu that was 75$ a person. Everyone left hungry and the it was only one small plate of galbi and one small plate of pork belly to share between 10+ people. We complained and got one more portion each but so dissatisfied. The same 75$ at another korean bbq would give one plate of galbi a person at least.

The staff seemed depressed and not attentive, the bathrooms was dirty - i mean there was still poop in the toilet from how many people before?? 

To be honest, i been here 2 years ago and i dont know what happened, menu has changed, staff changed over, prices are outrageous, and portions are made for small children.

We came here for a birthday dinner. They offered prefix menu which is $75 per person. We literally got one tiny piece of beef and pork belly. The amount of food is sooo small. Don't order the fried chicken, it's so salty, and not well cooked. Won't come again.

I'd never say no to an opportunity to try a new Korean bbq spot. The indoor dining is great, clean, and very spacious. The staff was delightful and very thorough with all the items we ordered. 

The fried chicken were amazing! Would definitely come back just for that. The seafood pancake could be more packed. We ordered short rib, shrimp, and mushrooms to grill for the table. I wish we had the opportunity to grill it ourselves - I feel like that's the charm of Kbbq and it just felt wrong having some one do it for us hibachi style. I also would prefer to have the bbq items pre-seasoned (or give us the option of how we would like to season it by spice level) - although not bad - just tasted sort of bland. 

The bibimbap was a miss.  The entire bottom of the bowl was full of crispy inedible rice and I'd prefer to have it come out and mixed for me. It was just too messy to mix it ourselves for the entire table as you have to do it standing up and the bowl is really hot.

We ate outside and had the best time. The frozen Joto Sake cups were amazing. That and their friend chicken made it a good night. Because we were outside we didn't do bbq (you'll need to book an indoor res for that) but they still had good options to eat. It's a really special place in Brooklyn that serves Korean. The only other good Korean option I can think of is Haenyeo in Park Slope but that isn't kbbq.

lovely spot! beautiful decor and very unexpected! felt like we were in a sauna.. food was overall 8/10.. we had the seafood pancake 10/10, Kimchi Bokkeumbap 10/10,  Galbi 9/10 abit on the chewy side for me, Samgyupsal 2/10 favorless and pricey, Mochi Sizzle 10/10,Thai Tea Sherbert 3/10.. will come back for other dishes! drinks 9/10,  ended up with bill of $200 for 2 ppl

Wonderful dining experience, beautiful 
Minimalistic interior, and high quality food! 
Love that they have a mushroom option for the bbq. Get the sea food "corn dog" !!!!

Dined for the first time at Insa tonight. Just as a reward to my daughter for being a wonderful, helpful and selfiless young lady. The experience was beyond words. We were warmly greeted and attended to by Siobhan, who I found out had created an excellent cocktail called "three lil women" and easy but strong drink. My daughter had a pear lemonade which was equally as delicious. The bbq banchan, meat dumplings and kimchi fried rice. The meal came with an accompaniment of sides which were extremely tasty and well paired. The ambience is warm and comfy. Highly recommended.

They don't get 1 star from me either but this is the minimum yelp gives any business so...
First and foremost, this is a wanna be kbbq place to put it mildly. This is a half hearted attempt at korean cuisine. This is not a homemade style with the taste of korean mom's or grandmom's touch. I can't believe they are portraying themselves ever so proudly as a korean restaurant across social media platforms. This is like a get money quick and run scheme riding on kpop bandwagon because it is a popular trend among young and hip crowds. I'm ashamed to have known this restaurant and even suggest it to my friends to try this place since we all live in Brooklyn and sometimes don't feel like trekking to ktown in the city or to flushing for fine authentic and solid korean food. Their food sucks period. Idont care if covid19 puts a damper on business bottomeline but this sh*t is a borderline false advertising and wasteful of your money. Definitely  one of the top worst restaurants i have ever been to in my life. It is a popular concept but poorly executed and good service doesn't make up for bad food. Please hire a proper korean cook/s to deserve my hard earned money.

Popped in by accident and it was the best accidental fine ever ! Owners and staff were beyond friendly and accommodating, the food was spectacular. I can't wait to be able to utilize the karaoke rooms in the future. I'll surly be back!

Stopped by with six friends for a Birthday dinner. The service with Sunny was awesome. The food and drinks were above expectations. Flavors that danced in your mouth. Covid safe you will not be disappointed.
Soy glazed shrimp with crispy noodles delivered quickly, BUT, I wish it never came!!..Shrimp so overcooked and tough as to be inedible.  Threw shrimp out and ate the noodles.

My husband and I have dinner here in their outside dining area every week. Siobhan and the team here are as warm and kind as you'll ever experience in service and hospitality. So much fun, so thoughtful. My favorite time was when it started drizzling and they brought umbrellas out for everyone seated. 

Besides that the drinks and the food are excellent every week. Pickled daikon (mu) is a favorite to nosh on the side as well as the bibimbap. Actually, in the over 5 years that we've been eating here, we've never had a bad dish. Not once. Not sure what Taurat's excellence bar is, but they are welcome to go somewhere else and leave the raving INSA fans to enjoy their food and the excellent service here. More tables for us. And happier less snobbish people around us too! No need for that energy here. If that means I'm lowbrow, I'm proudly so.

If you want a fun dining experience, good food, great service, order from here to take home or while it's still warm enough sit outside and enjoy.

I'm not a Korean BBQ connoisseur, but I know what tastes good and the food here was pretty damn good. This was a packed spot and was hard to get reservations. My friend and I were lucky enough to know someone who knew the chef who was able to get us a table and a room for karaoke after. We had the oxtail and the bbq beef and it was all wonderful. Not to mention, everyone there looked super cool for school (including the staff). Very downtown BK vibes. The interior was dark, so I'm sure it probably looks a little less nice with the lights on, but as for my experience in the dimly lit space... it was just ambient lighting and was more than suitable for me. Not my first Korean BBQ jaunt, and certainly not my last!

Price is only an issue in the absence of service/quality and for that reason, I write this. If you've never been to Korean bbq, then you must know it's a cuisine ideal for an indoor dining experience. It's sorta pivotal to eat the meat and veggies fresh, some sesame oil, salt, pickles,  etc. So kudos and best wishes to Insa for trying to thrive through this unusual circumstance of Covid as a restaurant. I truly mean that. 

With that being, I had a feeling I was in for a suspect KBBQ dining experience when I saw both soju and sake on the menu. If you don't know the difference, then this place is ideal for you. It's like asking for spaghetti meatballs at a sushi restaurant. Secondly, as much praise as Insa rightfully gets for trying to survive in an unusual global circumstance, they don't get absolution for providing an inferior, abysmal product. Especially at $27 for galbi (their version is basically beef teriyaki strips over rice, a few radishes and pickles) when there are places in the city for around $19-$22 providing significant quality product. Hell, as much as BK shits on Queens, I can recommend better places in flushing. 
We ordered two plates: Galbi & shrimp angel noodle pasta (their version is some teriyaki flavor sauce on a bed of hard cooked pasta and respectably seasoned shrimp). It tasted as bad as it sounds. Took about 5 minutes worth of bites and discussed a graceful exit plan. Covered our plates with the disposable plates provided and paid the bill ($53.00+ gratuity). 

As someone who grew up in KTown Los Angeles, I feel like I'm somewhat qualified for this rather blunt review: this isn't a Korean bbq restaurant. I recommend walking 1/2 a block to Ghanet on Douglas & 4th for a truly excellent Ethio dining experience.
The Insa Fried Chicken is insane!!! My boyfriend and I love this place. Great atmosphere inside. Very accommodating amid COVID. Quick preparation and same quality food.

2nd time to this place and experience is still superb!
Went on a Saturday night around 10pm and place was packed! Only waited like 2 minutes to be seated.

Service: Decent, the waitress was attentive in the beginning and the BBQ server was on point. Towards the end of the meal the waitress got busy and we felt like she forgot about us with asking us how we were doing, the bill and dessert. But understandably she had a big group to attend to.
Environment: Loud and noisy, it was a full house that night. They also have private karaoke rooms in the back
Decor: Rustic with a bar separated to the side in another room, bench-like seating area, has a cute entrance with coat hangers on the wall before you check in with the hostess
Drinks: Jujube Mine which is whiskey and jujube with bitters and a jasmine hot tea which came in a really cute pot that looks like a French press
Food: Seafood pancake (Haemul Pajeon) , tofu and vegetables bibimbap in stone bowl (Dolsot Bibimbap), marinated kalbi short ribs (Yangnyum Galbi) and pork belly (Samgyeopsal) BBQ order for the table. Also got the coconut sorbet with candied gingers as dessert. 

Galbi was delicious and very flavorful, the little vegetables on the side was cute and some were pretty good. The vegetable bibimbap was yum and came in a big portion and being in the stone bowl it stayed hot throughout the entire meal. Seafood pancake was crispy on the outside and soft on the inside very delicious and juicy. Wasn't fond of the coconut sorbet, the candied gingers was very overwhelming and could barely taste the coconut. 
They gave us the wrong pork belly order, instead of the thick sliced one that we asked for they gave us the thin sliced pork belly and charged us for the thick sliced amount which was 4 dollars more.

Overall? Still the best spot in park slope, service could be a little better and attentive.

We came with a party of four last Tuesday and it was absolutely delicious: I had a very refreshing cocktail to start, I believe it's called Eastern Lights. The bulgogi and brisket were delicious, as was the jap chae and tartare, and we got a vegetable side of yu choy, which is like if bok choy and broccoli rabe mated. If you like greens, this is a must-get. The ban chan was great as well. 
I've read a lot of complaints on here about the price and service. It is not cheap, true, but the pricing is on their website and their menu, there's no hidden surprise. If it's more than you wish to spend, cool, there are many places in K-town that will work for you. As for our experience service-wise, our server was very pleasant and attentive, and the gentleman running the food is exceptionally sweet. I have a serious allergy to certain types of shellfish and he was so helpful in pointing out what I needed to avoid and in taking care of us in general. We will definitely be back.
Must admit I'm Korean bbq addict lol , love the decor and that they cook it for you :) . The meat selection wasn't very long but was limited to only yummy selection

To be perfectly honest, you could probably find better Korean food and karaoke in k-town for cheaper, however, Insa was very accommodating. I came here for my friend's birthday dinner on a Wednesday night and the place was pretty much empty.  They did not take reservations because it was only a group of six people. Some of our group was late so they sat us in the bar. The waiter was very attentive in answering all of our questions. Per his recommendation we ordered six items:  fried rice cakes, seafood pancake,bibimbap,fried dumplings, chicken wings, and bulgolgi. Our whole group agreed the food was just okay and wasn't hitting. Maybe their barbecue is better? I did like that the rice cakes were kind of crispy unlike other Korean places. Also, I found it weird that didn't give any rice to eat with the side dishes which I thought was normal for Korean places. Their karaoke usually closes earlier but they still let us use it so that was great!

Occasion : my friend's B-day dinner. Group of 10. The decor here is very sleek and minimalist. Festive atmosphere. The place insisted that all of us be there for our 8:30pm reservation. Few of us hanged out by the bar. When the time came, they were still able to sit us minus one person.

Drinks:  The most impressive cocktail was the Jade Emperor (we got 4 of them) It was made from Pisco, matcha (not a strong flavor) with a strong cucumber taste. Very refreshing! Eastern Lights were also a hit for those preferring to drink vodka. 

Food: We were confused at first about how to proceed. All credit goes to our server Justin who guided each of us with our choices. We all ordered an item for BBQ and shared family style. Food was made tableside with accompanied side dishes. He gave good suggestions. Here is what we loved from the menu:

-THE RIBEYE. It ran for $45. But it was so flavorful, so tender. 
-Beef Tartare. Surprisingly so so delicious! Probably my favorite dish
-Yangnyum Galbi. Beef short rib. A good option after the rib, had a BBQ flavor. 
-Dolsot Bibimbap with bulgogi. Came in a good portion!
-Japchae. Loved the glass noodles!
-Samgyeopsal. thinly sliced pork belly. looked like bacon. still good!

Cons: the biggest cons is obviously the price. Our bill came down to a whopping $596. And it's not like I walked out of there with a super full belly. Obviously not an everyday type of place to eat.

Our first waiter was nice but then he left and we had different waiter and waitresses each time. The waiter that took our order didn't put some certain orders in. When asking our next waitress if our missing drink and food was coming out, she replied as if it came out already and that we lied or something. Like "Are you sure this isn't your second drink?" The food is over priced. I'm thinking, I paid over $100 for literally two bites of food. The BBQ meat had no flavor! Also there were no sauces to dip. The only dish I actually enjoyed was their ramen noodle. I'll only becoming back for the seafood ramen noodle other than that no. I then put in another order for the seafood noodle and drink and that never came out either. I asked the waiter if he's going to get me my drink and he told me to give him a minute and he never came back. *NOTICE* I said waiter then waitress then waiter because everyone keep changing! I think the management sucks.

Good food - EXTREMELY UNCOMFORTABLE ABOUT PAYMENT

Came to Insa recently with a party of six. We were seated a little after our reservation time and waited at the nice bar area for a bit. When we were ushered to the table I asked the bartender if he'd like me to close out and he told me they'd just move the drink to our table bill. I wanted to be sure he'd get the tip, but ok. 

All the food we ordered was good - sweet potato noodles, fried chicken, bibimbop (bulgogi and tofu), with the exception of the "veggie fritters" which were an oily mess. Our server was pleasant but she definitely oversold how much food we needed when we asked how many dishes to order. It took a while to get the check, but the restaurant was busy and we understood why the server was overwhelmed. After several attempts, we told another server we had a reservation for karoake and didn't want to lose the room, and we then got the dinner bill. As we were sorting out who owed what (two designated drivers in the group so we didn't want them to overpay), we were told to move to the private room and pay there. Not once or twice, but three times the server asked if we were ready to pay and I explained we were trying not to make our non-drinking friends overpay. I don't know if she thought six grown women were about to run out on a check (and a room we had for 2 hrs), but she then sent in a male employee who turned off the music, turned on the lights and gave us a new bill with automatic gratuity on it. We were all very embarrassed by this, but wanted to get some singing on, so we took the new bill and sorted it out. That incident really put a damper on things. 

There's a button in the karaoke room you're told to push if you want to order anything. In two hours we were able to get a server to come by twice. At least one of those times someone had to go out and flag someone down because no one responded to the call button. This  was not a bunch of drunken college kids getting wild and wanting drinks every five minutes - but two rounds of drinks in 2 hrs? When they brought the bill for drinks we tried to split it two ways (didn't want to repeat the earlier incident and get a nasty attitude again) and we were told they couldn't run any credit cards already run that night. That seemed more than fishy so I just charged it all to my own card. 

In the end I wouldn't recommend Insa to anyone unless the service and payment issues are resolved. Our group was respectful and responsive to everyone there and we were made to feel like we were trying to sneak out somehow.

Wow, capitalism sings a sad song. Booked a reservation for 12 people for a holiday party for 12/11/19 (confirmed on 11/14/19), we had some of our team from California flying out just for the party. They called me on the night of 11/25/19 at 9:15PM probably hoping I wouldn't answer, to tell me they had someone who wanted to do a buyout of the entire restaurant so they had to cancel our reservation. As a fellow business owner, I can't imagine a worse example of customer service.

The worst part is that I found out from a friend that it was their company that did the buy-out and I know that they requested to do the buy-out the day that they canceled my reservation. Meaning a better opportunity came along and the restaurant decided it was a better fiscal decision to screw over all the other reservation holders so they could make a couple of extra bucks.

#sad

This was my first korean bbq experience and it didnot disappoint. I went here for a team celebration and we tried all sorts of things. For drinks we got the dragon bowl which has cinnamon, orange and a lot of alcohol. Super tasty and packs a punch. For appetizers we tried the dumplings and pancakes. I didnot try either but everyone seemed to enjoy them.

My favorite dish was the sweet potato noodles with vegetables and egg. They did make it vegetarian  and were a good portion size. The main for me was the seasonal vegetable bbq. They did take care to change the tray and use fresh tools. A lot of the sides were vegetarian as well. My favorite was the maitake mushroom (no surprises here!).

Post our dinner, we had booed a karaoke room. It was new for me that korean bbq + karaoke are a thing. The service in the room was fast and they did bring us our drinks on time. I do want to point out that they did take care of our allergies and dietary restrictions pretty well (despite a large group).

I went here for my birthday and loved it! It's a cute vibe, preferably for date night. However to the food is a bit pricey. We did family style and shared the servings. It's definitely more than enough food, I was stuffed! The scallion pancake is bomb. I would definitely go back. 

Service: 5/5
Food: 5/5
Atmosphere: 5/5

I hadn't been here since it first opened up and I am glad I gave this place another try after so long. I came in on Saturday a little after Insa opened for the day. We were able to be easily seated. We ordered the tteobbokki, Insa fried chicken (half), and kimchi jigae. The tteobbokki was pretty decent, but not amazing. The kimchi jigae was also good, but it lacked that spicy omphff at the end of each bite. The standout was the Insa fried chicken. The chicken was really crispy and the sauce was delicious. Definite a must order item. Overall, I am pleased I came here. The prices are a little bit higher than other places, but I will definitely come again to try the other items!

I lived in Korea and I LOVE KOREAN food. Unfortunately, I felt this food was more "KOREAN inspired" for Americans taste sensitivities. For me, the food was flat! For my guests who had never eaten KOREAN food, they didn't think it was that impressive... especially when you factor in the cost. Yeah, I'll brave the cold next time and take my friends into Manhattan for KOREAN food. One final thing... the kimchi was too fresh! I have always thought of Kimchi as being a highly honored food for Koreans. This kimchi lacked... a lot!

Came here on a Saturday night with a group of nine at 7 pm and didn't get seated until 11 pm. We went across the street to Threes, had some fries, slammed a couple beers and came back. I can tell you it was worth the wait...and I'm Korean! 

Im reading all these hater reviews saying "it's not authentic" "it's too expensive"... which compelled me to write my review... I know Korean food well, haters quit your whining. Sohui Kim is a trailblazer, what she is doing to educate the masses on Korean cuisine and make it accessible to a larger population deserves the respect of every Korean American, just but y her book Korean Home Cooking.  This place is great, been here 3 times now, and their bbq is solid, quality of banchan is solid and their spin on Korean food is well executed, with attention to detail. The ambiance is cozy yet festive, and the staff are friendly and attentive.
Cool vibe with nice lighting and layout of the restaurant. The vegan options of japchae and vegetable bibimbap (without the egg) were delicious, especially the japchae.

I came here for my birthday dinner wanting some filling Korean bbq. Seriously overpriced (see math below). We ordered the whole fried chicken, u choy, kimchi pancakes, short rib bbq (kalbi), pancetta Coreana, and Japchae. 

Fried chicken was pretty good, no complaints there. U choy was not bad, not mind blowing. Kimchi pancake was also fine but not revelatory. Japchae was lacking complexity. Banchan was alright, don't know if the kimchi was homemade. 

My big issue with this place was the bbq portion sizes, and portions sizes overall frankly (except chicken). They gave us maybe 6oz of short rib, which when cooked turns into about 4oz... and it cost $39! That's $160/lb for short rib... EXCUSE ME??? Short rib costs less than $10/lb at Whole Foods and the restaurants probably paying $6/lb or less. I don't appreciate that. The pancetta was like 6-8 THIN slices of bacon, tasted saltier than anything else, and cost over $25. I find it mildly insulting and I will not return.

I don't like being a hater, I only like to say nice things, but thought I should warn the people. I'd give it a one star but the chicken saved it.

I planned a bachelorette party here (9 girls). I am so glad I did. Insa exceeded my expectations. The food was excellent! Every single dish that came out we couldn't believe how tasty. We ordered a bunch of sharables for the table. Insa chicken, pork buns, beef rice bowls, bbq short ribs, seafood scallion pancake ( a favorite) and fried pork dumplings. Everything was seriously delicious. While it may not be the most authentic Korean bbq, it was great food!
The reason I didn't give 5 stars was because of the service. Our waiter could have been more attentive and friendly. I also noticed the wait staff talking and laughing together a lot which means they were not doing their jobs. That being said it was not terrible but could be improved. 
We ended the night with a private karaoke room which was such a blast! We had an amazing night at Insa and I totally recommend going with a group to celebrate!
It's not authentic Korean food at all. The food sucks and it's expensive. Would not recommend not come back to this place

So excited to finally have amazing korean food in the neighborhood. The bar and main dining room are beautifully designed in modern Korean form. The food - The korean fried chicken is the best I've ever had and the stews are rich with high quality ingredients. Will be back!

Went here yesterday and was pleasantly surprised but not overly impressed. Finding authentic Korean food in Brooklyn is pretty difficult and after being disappointed by several places (which won't be named), I was hoping this could become a go-to.

The food was decent but tasted very americanized. It seemed like the flavors were all a bit off, with the budae jjigae tasting too buttery and lacking the diverse range of flavors that a traditional korean budae jjigae offers. There was also supposed to be spam in it but didn't find any. The dubu kimchi was actually very good! There should be a slightly sweet element to the dish to balance out the spicy but overall, it was solid and I'd order this dish again. We got the yangyum galbi (shortrib) and while the meat was great, I found that there were several ingredients to a "ssam" that were missing. No scallion, the bean paste was more the consistency of a sauce than a paste, and we weren't given garlic or peppers to build out the wrap as most korean restaurants give. It's a solid 3/5 for the food as well. 

Service was great and appreciated how attentive the staff were. The overall decor was clean and minimal and I loved the skylight as it brought a lot of natural light into the restaurant. However, between the side "speakeasy" type bar, the karaoke, and the bbq grills, it seems like they're trying to offer/focus on too many things at once. As such, the overall experience seems to lack authenticity and grades overall at a solid 3/5.

RIP OFF. Wings are good tho

they are charging $75/bottle for bottles that you'd expect to be 1L but are half the size and should be $30. it's a fun time, but not worth the premium.

AMERICANIZED HORRIBLE KBBQ.... this place looks like an American dining hall with KBBQ grills randomly placed inside.  The service started off well until I ordered the yaki mandu.   The server then tried to correct me and said its yache.  I'm like I don't care how you Americans spell it I'm korean and its yaki and she got mad and then proceeded with the worst service afterwards.  Not one single korean works here so there is no authenticity.  This is just a RIP off of a culture and trying to make a profit of off them ...bad food, bad service, save your money and time.

Btw don tell a korean he is wrong about his own ethnicity and culture and then get pouty about it.

Took my young friend out to dinner to celebrate her high school graduation, she wanted to try something different and picked Korean BBQ - I have to say I am so glad she did and what truly made the experience was our server AVERY! He was amazing really walked us through the whole experience. Even though he himself doesn't eat meat he explained the menu and even let us cook with his assistance . After that the food was amazing and the desert was to  die for. We would recommend this place 100 times over.
Really fun place to eat! Food was great and we had a great time singing karaoke! We even had our 18month old with us in the karaoke room and still had a great time.

I love this Korean option in the neighborhood. It can get crowded so come early if you can. We got there right at 5pm when it opened and were able to get a table right away. This is a great place for groups as they have tables that can fit 8 or even 10. It is a big open space so good for kids and strollers. They allowed us to keep the stroller by table and they also have high chairs. Each table has a barbecue set up but you can choose to not do barbecue and just order a la carte. I loved their spicy squid udon noodles. Their udon was a bit like ramen but it was very tasty. The kids loved the food too. There is a separate area for karaoke with different rooms. They have a separate food and drink menu for those rooms. It seems like you would have to book those rooms quite in advance because they get filled up. The waitress was extremely nice and accommodating with the kids so that was great. Can't wait to come back!

My friends and I wanted to get Korean food but wanted to stay in the area, so we decided to go to Insa. We were surprised that this place was more Americanized than your typical kbbq place, which I don't necessarily think is a bad thing as long as the output is good.

First, let's start with the good things - the interior is aesthetically pleasing, with a big open space and plenty of sunlight when it's still light outside. I only tried one of their cocktails, the Stylish Tomato, which was decently strong but the taste wasn't overpowered by vodka so it was easy to drink.

The food was a hit or miss. We had the pork jowl that barely tasted like anything, but the pork belly was great! Tasty with the right amount of fat. The portions are unfortunately small for the price. I also had the soondubu and requested it to be extra spicy, but it was equivalent to a regular level of spice at other restaurants in Ktown. It also had a distinguishable taste of tomatoes that I've noticed more "Americanized" Korean restaurants tend to have in their soondubu.

The service was less than stellar. The servers here stand at your table and focus on heating and cutting your meat. I guess you could take that as being attentive, but I find it inefficient especially because our server was moving at a snail's pace! I had to resist myself from volunteering to take over because he was moving SO slowly. When he came over with our second plate of meat, before he started putting anything on the grill I quickly asked for a drink menu but he got snappy saying he'd have to get someone else because he "has to focus on grilling" - it's not that serious, buddy. There was another time we wanted to get someone's attention but there were 5 servers standing together having a conversation and not paying attention at all despite them all facing towards the tables.

Despite the service, I don't necessarily think Insa is bad. It's just not that great. I wouldn't think of coming back here again though unless we're somehow physically stuck in Brooklyn and can't get to Manhattan where the good stuff is.

We had a reservation for 8 for eating in the dining area, and then karaoke afterward. They have a tiki style bar area that we waited at for rest of our party to show up, as they don't seat until you have your full party.

After being seated and server came to take our order, a few subtle things started to happen. The server proceeded to walk away to attend to another table, halfway when we were making our order and deciding between items.

We ordered their house soju and they gave us a bottle that was 3 quarters finished. We let them know and they didn't even realize and were confused why we wanted to return the bottle, and we had to point it out more clearly to them. Then a different server came by and asked whether there was a problem with the bottle. We were surprised that there was such a lack of communication between the staff, it's clear that it was already drank by a different group before us. We haven't even started eating or drinking yet.. 

The poor service continued as they gave us an order for a different table. We had to correct them again.

In the end we tried to appreciate the food and drink, but their house made soju was actually disgusting. I'm not really sure what we expected, especially since it wasn't flavored soju or anything. 

The meat quality was mediocre. We soon realized that the only reason why people came to this establishment was that they probably live too far from ktown manhanttan - because the price was the same for subpar meat quality.

I highly recommend against coming here if you are able to just go to ktown. This place also requires advanced reservation for weekend nights, I guess since it'd the only kbbq in the entire area.

The karaoke was decent. They have an app you can use for song selection.

Overall I would say if you live in bklyn it's probably an okay choice, but not worth trekking to if you're coming from Manhattan.

While the food here is definitely watered down for the Western palate, overall this restaurant presents a good variety of Korean traditional dishes in an accessible manner. While the stews were by no means as spicy or strongly flavored as the ones I've eaten in Korea, they felt hearty and satisfying.  The banchan were a bit on the paltry side--when we finished all of our little plates and what amounted to about three bites of *very mild* kimchi (a travesty for a table for four) our server asked us rather dubiously if we really wanted more. Um, YES!  You do have to ask and pay for rice separately, which is a bit odd in a Korean restaurant, even of the NYC variety. Overall, the pancakes and other share dishes are worth trying and the atmosphere is casual and lively. We especially liked the seafood pancake. I wish I could say the service was good, but it was almost impossible to flag down a server for more drinks, etc. I felt like I was constantly trying to make eye-contact with someone who thought I was below her notice...
Singing, drinking, eating! Had a wonderful karaoke night. Service was amazing, food came out promptly. Food was very tasty. Will come back.

Very cool decor, like a Korean sauna. Service staff were attentive and friendly. Food was absolutely delicious - the best seafood scallion pancakes I've ever had. The grilled marinated short rib was also very good. Fun for groups of friends, with very long tables.

Recently went here for the third time and had an even better meal than my previous visits. For one thing, the portion size has increased, which had been a problem -- especially for this mom feeding a starving college kid. The roasted meats are terrific, but so are the appetizers, which are made with as much care as the main courses. Be adventuresome! The service is always great, the wait staff friendly and helpful, and the wait for tables pretty normal, even on a busy night. My only gripe is that -- as someone nearing 60 -- sitting on a bench at table is tiresome. Being able to lean against the back of the chair as I sip my sour ale and nibble roasted brisket dipped in hot sauce would be heaven. A few chairs, please?

Came here for a friends birthday party, the place was packed when we arrived but got seated on time. I opted out the bbq portion and tried almost all the appetizers with the group and it was a good decision. The fried chicken was pretty good except the part where the sauce was too salty for me, the blood sausage tasted plain, but overall a very nice modern place, the karaoke was a little pricey in my opinion but still had a good time.

I went to Insa to celebrate a milestone birthday with a small group of friends. The food was good and the karaoke was fun! However, every single person who works there from the waiters to the busboys both in the restaurant and karaoke room is soooooo rude and angry. They are heartless impatient zombies who can't even crack a smile. It was crazy! It's really unfortunate that the staff is so terrible. Also, when I made my reservation I requested a specific thematic karaoke room as per the hostesses suggestion and I bought decorations etc to match the theme. When I got to the restaurant the host told me that I was moved to a different themed room and someone else was using the room that I had specifically reserved. So disappointing!

The hub and I were so bummed when Moim in Park Slope closed a few years back.  That was our go-to neighborhood spot for Korean comfort food.  Thank goodness a new option emerged in the Gowanus area right around the same time...Insa. 

We've dined at Insa numerous times now and we often bring guests (especially out-of-towners) here for dinner, most recently a week ago.  The food is always yummy and satisfying.  It all starts with a round of banchan, small dishes of various sorts (kimchi, cucumber, cuttlefish, spinach, eggplant, beans) you can nibble on while waiting for your meal.  They will bring you extra if there's one you particularly like. 

If it's just the two of us, our standard dinner order includes:

-- Dolsot Bibimbap with bulgogi.  You want to get this hot stone pot version so the rice component gets nice and crispy. 

-- Jap Chae, because who doesn't love noodles?

-- Budae Jjigae.  This is a phenomenal spicy stew that we just can't get enough of.  Trust me and get it.  Note: It's not always on the menu.  Our back-up soups are the Kimchi Jjigae and the newly-discovered-by-us Dwenjang Jjigae.  There's another soup with dumplings that I intend to try too.  Bottom line: yummy soups here. 

We've tried other things that we felt were fine, but not the best examples, including scallion pancake, dumplings and at-table bbq.  For the latter, we enjoy the bbq restos in K-Town better.  Granted the upside here is that you don't reek of smoke when you leave as they use gas grills instead of charcoal. 

Getting into Insa can be tricky, as it's quite popular.  Unfortunately, they don't take rezzies for parties under six.  They do take walk-in's and sometimes you get lucky. If not and there is a wait, they have a cocktail lounge area where you can hang out and order drinks and food to, if you like.  We aren't blown away by the cocktails or wine options, but there's a decent variety.  If the bar area is too crowded, you can cross the street and enjoy a beer at Three's Brewing while you wait. 

The dining room at Insa is a relaxing open space with long communal tables.  Each has a grill component for those who order at-table grilled meats.  The wait staff/servers tend to be friendly. 

If you're feeling crazy, you can rent one of the karaoke rooms behind the dining area. 

Go to Insa.  (I'm drooling now, just thinking of it.)

Not what I expected after hearing the Bon Appetite podcast episode that featured the owner/chef in terms of the atmosphere, but the food we had was solid. The bartenders knew their sake, so bonus points for that. The one downside is that the menu is extensive which to us typically means small plates, but the portions were huge (hence the high prices). It would have been much more enjoyable if we could have tried more things, but we were full after just 2 dishes.

Food: 0/5
Drinks: 4/5
Service: 2/5
Atmosphere: 4/5

This is an Americanized Korean restaurant. Definitely save your money and go elsewhere. We ordered steak and beef along with other side dishes. Servers came around and cooked beef on one side and pork on one side. The guy cooking the beef was taking awhile to cook while the guy cooking the pork was cooking it very quickly. Little did we know, the pork came out UNCOOKED, still pink in the meat. The beef came out perfectly to medium - which was fine. Because the guy cooking the pork was cooking it so quickly, we had asked him to keep it on the grill little longer, but it was still pink. If it wasn't one or two pieces that was pink, it was the entire dish... 

I can live with beef undercooked, but pork? Definitely not. We let a different waitress know that our pork was still pink. She happily turned on the grill for us but did not help us re-cook it again nor did she mentioned to any of her colleagues. 

Overall, don't think I would come here again. Save your money and go to flushing - definitely more authentic there

Came here with a group of about 18-ish for a bachelorette party. The hostess ordered a bunch of different dishes which was all enjoyed (my pallet is more adventurous than the rest of the group so i would've loved to try more authentic stuff, ya know?)
Food came out promptly. kept us all very busy and satisfied until it was karaoke time.
I think we were singing for like +2hrs.... we stayed till they kicked us out lol
Great location for food and fun. Would love to go back (and buy the Insa cookbook)
Delicious food. Good service. The Karaoke room is nice and the sound system is great.

Solid Korean place in Brooklyn. 

Reservations were easy to make on resy. We were running late on Sunday early evening and they were saving our table. Seats and tables are nice wooden communal style. They have lots of private rooms for karaoke. I def want to go back for that. 

Now onto food. Marinated galbi was delicious. Good quality meat but expensive for little bit. Comparable to ktown. Also got the mushroom to grill which was delicious. 

Fried chicken was crispy and juicy on inside but the batter is too thick and puffy for my liking. Not double fried like usual Korean style. BUT the kids loved it so I barely even had any. Lol

The seafood pancake is the best I've ever had. Crispy outside and chewy on the inside. At first I was skeptical because it's pretty thick but thats because there's lots of stuff inside! But eat it hot. Once it cools down, not as good. 

Soon dubu was fine but had a thicker spicy sauce than Im used to. 

Banchan was fine. Nothing too special except I like the spicy cuttlefish or squid. 

Cumin ribs were yummy and very flavorful. Japchea was normal.

called to make a reservation they told me they didn't accept reservations i asked how long the wait was she said 30 minutes, i arrived 8 minutes later and then was told the next table was available was an hour and a half. then when i went online they in fact do accept reservations and the next available table was at 7:45 a half hour later. i don't care how good their food is their customer service sucks wish i could rate a big fat ZERO

Went here for bibimpap in a hot stone bowl and it was great, portions were large and came on a wooden plank. Yelp says it's $16.00, it's actually $19. The hostess and the waitress were rude. We didn't have our orders taken until 20 minutes after seating. My brother ordered seollungtang and it was a really sad dish. The waiter had misled him to think it was full of oxtail and a large bowl of soup when in reality it was one small oxtail in a "beef broth" aka salt and the water they boiled the oxtail in with some cut up scallions. That dish was $19 as well. Fortunately, the staff was able to rectify the situation and comp that particular meal in place of another bibimpap. The service was awful in the beginning and was better at the end. Unnecessary hassle at what would of been a good Thursday night dinner.
