Went here to celebrate​ national women's​ day with my BFF. The place​ is so welcoming. The tables are like lunch tables from elementary with a pit in the middle where the cook certain dishes. I had the crab stew which was delicious. The Mai Tai was strong and cook. Loved the coconut cup just ish it was real. Would definitely​ recommend​!!!

I'm so glad this place is walking distance.  The bar is so fun, the cocktails are great and the food delicious.  But the karaoke. Great book, nice rooms, prompt service. Where I go when I want to get my sing on.

I had to make a yelp account for the first time to say that if you're used to the portions of meat given at Korean bbq places in Ktown or Flushing in the city, I would not recommend spending your money here. My brother and I wanted to try since there was a snowstorm last night and we couldn't get into the city on time so we thought we would try a local place nearby. We were pretty disheartened to find that three pieces of meat cost around $30-49 and were overall disappointed with the quantity.

I believe if you order anything else off the menu you would get your money's worth but I am warning those who want more quantity to not go here for bbq and advise going to the city at all costs instead. That being said, I am giving two star instead of one because the food itself did taste great, and the waitress serving our table was incredibly sweet. Additionally, the ambiance and cleanliness were excellent, but it is unfortunate this was what the Brooklyn Korean bbq experience was like for us.
Terrific Korean bbq and a great vibe.  Service was spot on. Menu is quite extensive. All around great meal.

I'm giving three stars because I don't feel it's fair to judge a restaurant and karaoke joint on their cocktails and service alone, but because of those things I don't think I'm going to be back to try much else.

Back in 2017, I found out about Insa because they competed in the Bloody Mary Festival at Grand Prospect Hall. I voted for them! They had an amazingly original, umami packed Mary with candied sardines for garnish. Who knew I loved THOSE so much?? 

So when I came in I excitedly asked the bartender if they served that drink here.

I received a stony "no", with no eye contact. Then she left to busy herself with other things. Oooook, that's not a great start.

She did come over and take our drink order, so she must have asked what we wanted, but other than that didn't speak a word to us. I did ask her if they had karaoke (it was the first I had heard about it) she said "In the back". I asked if they ever had it at the bar, she pointed wordlessly at a sign to the side of the bar advertising it. She seemed to be in a funk, but was talking a bit to some people she knew in a corner who were having a great time. Whatever. The drinks were sugary and weak, we didn't get another round. Maybe she had something personal going on, everyone has a bad night, but the place ain't cheap and we were all smiles. Just try, ok? Or say you have laryngitis and can't talk, otherwise you're coming off seriously rude.

We ordered the bar snacks, seaweed with dried shrimp and some nuts. The seaweed was interesting, the nuts are just spiced nuts, I'd skip this. 

The setting is beautiful. It's got that cool speakeasy vibe outside, a warm red interior with velvet booths, lights, fishtank at the bar. Korean BBQ inside. Snazzy private karaoke booths in the back with disco lights and other things. Even the bathrooms are pretty.

This place is AMAZING! I have never been the biggest fan of Korean bbq and don't love the idea of cooking my own food, but this changed my view on everything. There were 6 of us and we ordered a bunch of appetizers to share ( which would've been more than enough without the meat to grill as our entrees)

Do NOT skip the scallion pancakes and fried chicken, both were the best things I had ever tasted! The bibimbap and bulgogi were also delicious. The nice thing about Insa is that for the meat the waiter actually handles it all, which made me feel a lot better about things actually being cooked. 

Overall, super fun and great food! Worth the wait!
Food was ok and a little overpriced. Service was slow/awkward. Just go to k-town...so much better

Simple review.  Service good. Nice social set up w the option to bbq at the table.  Had the spicy squid udon and fried meat dumplings.  Both were pretty good. Felt like the squid was inconspicuously placed in the dish and would have rather had bigger pieces. All in all a decent spot for bigger groups , but over priced in my opinion.

Came here for a birthday dinner. You can only make reservations online if you have a party of 6 or more FYI. We thoroughly enjoyed our food, drinks and service (the server Mel was so down to earth and helpful with recommendations).

For drinks I had the Jade Emperor which was very refreshing AND strong. We started with the dumplings which were tasty and the chicken wings. I'm trying very hard to be vegan but I have to admit that the sight of these wings (I don't even usually like wings) and the servers description of the meat falling off the bone made me try one. And it was the best chicken wing I've ever had.

For entrees my partner and I had the vegetarian bibimbop and the sweet potato noodles. I loved the sweet potato noodles and the bibimbop was good (in the hot bowl) if you like when rice gets crunchy. Sauce that came with was a bit too spicy for me. 

As a side note, the bar has such an appealing ambiance that I'm determined to come back for a drink!

Not sure why we ordered delivery from a karaoke spot, but in any case this review is only for the food...

It was OK (japchae, dumplings, and bulgogi bibimbap)... expensive for what it is. We may actually go here one day for karaoke, but not again for the food.

The first time my partner and I went to Insa, about a year ago, we loved it. Then we went back on New Year's Day and were disappointed by both the service and dishes. The Tteok Mandu Guk soup was under-salted, the meat in the mandu was bland. The Yache Twigim (crispy vegetable fritters) were tasty but a little greasy and too much batter. It would also be helpful for servers to indicate these are like long strips of tempura and not actually fritters. Service was really hit or miss. We often had to ask two different servers for something like an extra plate, or extra fork, etc. We had to wait about 35 minutes for the soups to arrive and the place wasn't even full. I will give Insa another try with the hope that maybe they were just having an off night.

Depending on my mood, I'll go to insa for different things. It's solid Korean food (the chef just released a cookbook which I'm super excited to learn how to cook). It has a fun atmosphere so it's good for a date and you can head to the cool tiki looking bar after, or if you're with a group of friends, get a private karaoke room to continue the night. I'll sometimes come on during off peak hours and work at the bar because it's pretty chill.  Staff is always friendly. I'll keep coming back!

Karaoke was absolutely baller and I would definitely return for that, but after going to Insa I feel like I have just experienced the Great Recession of 2009 all over again. I will not sugar coat this: this restaurant/karaoke bar hybrid is extremely expensive. The food I had was good: vegetarian bibimbap and vegetarian dumplings but I just don't think the price was worth it. The drinks I got were extremely strong but still not enough bang for my buck. I would probably just go straight for the karaeoke room without drinks or food. Now for the positive, the kareoke room was super fun with an incredible song selection. There was a call button that we could use and have our very kind wait person come and help us at a moment's notice. The bathrooms were very clean. This place is also very close to Barclay's Center-Atlantic Avenue so you can arrive swiftly from Manhattan or Long Island or Queens if you feel like it.
Great food and cocktails! Recommend the blood sausage. Can get busy, but not too bad of a wait.

This place would make a nice non-intimate date spot for first time meet-ups and such.  Imagine getting to know someone new with a blue flame and pre-marinated meats or veggies (no judgement) providing you with all the "so what do you want to talk about" fuel you need to pull through.  The food here is pretty good, not great, but I would come back to try other options as well. I would have preferred to do the cooking myself as the server left the steak a little too rare at first. I've been to Korean spots like this where they turn the grill on and let you do your own thing. Here they stand over you until it's done and then turn the grill off and serve it to you.  I had to have her come back and re-light the grill to cook it for a minute or two longer.  Once they bright your food they kind of go ghost for a bit and you may have to flag them down if you need something else.  The white rice has a distinct flavor that pairs well with everything. The tofu is a bit bland so vegetarians and vegans be warned.  Some of the other accompanying dishes area quite delectable so that makes up for the few misses.  The hit of the meal is the fried chicken. It's pretty amazing, a little bit on the salty side but tasty nevertheless.

Come in for a pleasant experience.
This place is good if you have extra money in your pocket to waste. The service is not good and the food is not authentic korean barbecue. Definitely overpriced as well considering the portions.

The people here are disinterested in servicing. They don't really respond to you when you talk to them. They just kind of nod their head. The food is too expensive for the portion you receive. We ordered about 5 dishes and a tea and it was about $250. They cook the food for you on the grill but they burnt one of the dishes beyond recognition and it was completely inedible. The taste isn't particularly special. It's definitely not authentic. The side dishes are so-so. It's like a trap for white people who aren't experienced with Korean food. I doubt I'll come back.
This place is always top notch and I rarely hand out 5 star reviews. Do the BBQ, it's so fun. The tteokbokki should not be missed, nor the fried chicken or seafood pancake.
one of my favorite spots in BK! amazing cocktails and food. great service. karaoke rooms in the back. always have a fun time at Insa... :-)

Food and ambience at INSA are first rate. Interesting, tasty, well spiced and enjoyable. Have had dinner in both the restaurant and barroom and both are comfortable.  The restaurant us spacious and nmhs separate rooms for.karaoke. service us very good.

Our dining experience at Insa was a "mixed bag".  The food was good; the location convenient; our server bad.

It was my first time at the restaurant.  My family had frequented it many times, having a good experience each time.

The Gowanus restaurant's decor was modern simplicity.  There was a separate, small Karaoke Room with glitzy lighting covering all the walls and cushy seats.

The menu had less choices than other restaurants in the Tri-State area featuring Korean cuisine.  But there were an adequate number of entrees to meet our needs.  We placed an order with our server, which included wine.

The banchan consisted of 5-6 dishes.  It was tasty.  But a little more would have been appreciated.  

After what seemed to be way too much time, we asked our server about the wine.  She gave us a strange look and returned shortly afterwards with the glasses.   There was no apology or acknowledgement of the delay.  I had the Cabernet, which was good.

My Grandson and I ordered the Bibimbap with Bulgogi.  A different server, who my family was familiar with, brought our selections.  They were both Doisot Bibimbap.  She was very pleasant and immediately took away the incorrect dishes.  

When the familiar server returned with the correct entrees, my daughter in law told her that "things seemed to be a little out of sorts today", referring to the demeanor and performance of our server.  Shortly afterwards our server came to the table and not very pleasantly said "Is everything all right?"

My son ordered Boseot Modeum, from the BBQ section of the menu.  It looked fabulous and is a "must try" for my next visit.  The Bibimbap was also very good.

I would definitely recommend the restaurant in hopes that the reader of this review has a different server.

Came here on a date last night. It was the two of us on a Sunday night at 6:30. The wait was 45 minutes (They don't take reservations!) BUT they were very kind to inform us they had service at the bar.

I excitedly jumped at the chance. When you first walk in, there's a little window that peaks into the bar/lounge area -- it's red, lush, and visually my aesthetic. 

There were a few seats at the side bar, but we were so crazy lucky there was an entire BOOTH open! It feel like a dream, we had skipped the whole line and found this hidden gem. So if it's crowded when you go, seriously see if you can swap to the bar. We skipped a group of five that could have easily fit in the booth.


The bar area is waiterless, but the bar is 2 steps away and the food is delivered to you anyway.

We had the gogi mandu fried, tteokbokki, and bossam.

My favourite was the Gogi Mandu, amazing flavour and just the right level of crispy. Everything was great too. It was nice to go out and enjoy every aspect of the night.

Our cocktails were fabulous, I recommend the Sun&Moon.

It's worth the trek if you're not from the neighbourhood. I would love to come back.

This review is just for the bar.

I popped into Insa on a whim to grab a drink with my fiancé. I've been hearing about it for a while and had to see for myself! 

My first impression of Insa was "wow." It's pretty unassuming from the street, but once you enter it's just such a cool space, particularly the bar area that has kinda a 60s Asian lounge vibe. Super cool. The restaurant area looked great too. Simpler with long tables for bbq.

We had a cocktail each and shared an order of dumplings. The dumplings weren't the best I've had but they were very good. The cocktails were delicious and super well balanced. Mine has green tea and was so refreshing. I'd order it over and over!

Definitely stop in and check Insa out. I really enjoyed the bar here but will for sure be back for a full meal!

Not traditional Korean barbecue but they have a bunch of karaoke rooms where you can sing your heart out. There's better Korean food elsewhere, but it's close by and not horrible.

This place definitely sticks out among the surrounding hipster Brooklyn bars and restaurants - and thank god it does! There's a separate dimly lit bar area with lots of character perfect for a date. There's also an open kitchen looking out into a very spacious dining room filled with lots of cafeteria style tables that have stove tops for cooking your food.

While I didn't do the BBQ, the food was tasty and the service was good. I ordered the Japchae and my friend got the bibimbap with bulgogi beef. Both were large portions and we were quite satisfied with our dishes.

Staff was friendly and didn't bother us until we were ready for the check. 

NOTE: 20% GRATUITY IS BAKED INTO THE PRICE.

Food was okay, service was decent...but WHY NOT include the 20% (which is really  22%) on the menu price? Really a turn-off and a form of bait and switch. Really unfortunate when you're food is just good enough, and your main selling point is location Back to K-Town and Flushing for the real deal.

The food was ok, if a little overpriced. When you get the bill, you find theres an "administrative fee" that they say is 20 percent but is really 22 percent because ( even though they print the receipt as if the fee is not taxed, it is)   

Thats nonsense.if you want a no tipping restaurant, include it in the prices. 

They also wont take more than 4 credit cards... for no specific reason. 

All of this is completely unacceptable. I dont know who came up with this but ill never spend another dime here.

This review is for Karaoke ONLY

Came here with a gang of friends for a late night karaoke session and just wasn't a big fan of the staff. I think the experience is typically fun and fine when you are surrounded by your friends being a wild crowd, but I just felt that service was lacking a tad bit.

The food ranges from very good to excellent and the service is charming and skilled.  My main issue here that the prices seem to be about 20% higher than they should be ($15 for a small order of Kimchi Mandoo Dumplings) then they add 20% to the bill for everyone to have a living wage. So far I am on board. Then... there are mixed messages about tipping an additional amount.  There is no place for a tip on the credit card slip and the bill indicated that gratuities are not expected.  However, the staff seems to expect a gratuity and will even show you how to add it to your bill.  The menu does not make the issue any clearer. They need to send a direct message on this issue.

If you've ever been to a Korean BBQ restaurant in Korea Town you may just ask yourself, "why am I paying this much for incredibly mediocre food?" The service was good and waitstaff was very friendly but it's a pretty hard pill to swallow to pay $30 to watch someone burn 13 shrimp right before your very eyes. Why did I just pay $15 for 7 dumplings that are in no way better than a frozen gyoza I could make at home?

Ambience is great and I bet the Karaoke is fun too but also way overpriced compared to what you can find elsewhere in the city.

The restaurant was full of white Brooklynites and tourists who had seemed like they'd never had Korean food before.

The quality of this place really plummeted. I had a great time several months ago. The food was decent for Brooklyn and the atmosphere was fun. I came back here recently and what a mess. The wait was an hour, but the host made us wait 2 hours while there were MULTIPLE EMPTY TABLES that were open for more than 30 mins (maybe because we were a group of 2).  After prodding the host (who was actually the rudest manager) he eventually seats us at one of the empty tables. The service was poor; our waiter got our order wrong and we were rushed through our meal (in and out in 45 mins). At the end of the bill I was reminded of the MANDATORY 20% service fee,which is reasonable at other fancier establishments, but not for the service we got. What a waste of 200 dollars. Work on your game Insa, don't be lazy cuz you're the only Korean restaurant on the block.

The food was definitely good, but our night was ruined by an incredibly rude employee.  It's difficult to communicate tone in a review.  All I can say is that this bartender spoke to our group as if we were disobedient children.  From the moment we walked in and asked about drinks, she acted as if it was annoyance to have us there.  We then adjusted a lamp shade at our table because it was in my friend's eyes, and she snapped at us from across the bar that we shouldn't turn it off or touch it.  She could have easily said, "excuse me, but can I help you with something?" and we would have explained the situation but she chose to be angry, and boy, did she let us know it!  Perhaps we were wrong to touch the light, but I've been in the NYC restaurant business (as a server) for over 15 years, and no matter how wrong my customer is, I would never treat them the way this bartender treated us.  She didn't even have the decency to come to our table to speak to us but rather yelled across, from behind the bar.  It was embarrassing and made everyone in the room uncomfortable.  It's unfortunate because our group decided that, although the food was good, and the rest of the waitstaff, bus boys, hostess and manager were professional, this unprofessional bartender ruined our chances of ever wanting to return.

I had to organize a fairly large group dinner (~19 people) on an extremely abbreviated time frame, and Insa came to the rescue. Management was extremely responsive as we worked out the details, and we got everything lined up in under a week. While that alone would earn high praise, the actual dining experience was was also very good. 
- Large group menu options got unanimous high marks
- Good price point for food value ($75/person prix fix menu option)
- Attractive dining space (we got two long tables in a row). I was a little worried about the lack of a private area option, but it was a lively room so we didn't feel like we were discomfiting other patrons. 
- The on-site karaoke options were extremely convenient - your group can just slide into a room and start singing as the eating and drinking die down.
- Extremely warm and competent onsite management who rolled with a couple of last second curve balls we had regarding headcount and dietary issues with great aplomb. 

Overall a really good experience. I'm looking forward to going back personally to explore the menu more, and an excellent option for a larger group event.
Amazing Korean Fried Chicken, K-BBQ is delicious and seafood pancake was awesome. Great cocktails and will def make the trip out to BK again for this one

Been here twice so far.
Definitely not "traditional" Korean bbq, but I do like the little twists.
The service is great, food is decent and overall a great atmosphere. Very open space.

Insa does not fit into the category of KTown restaurants in Manhattan with the essential bbq, stews, and soju. The menu here is more adventurous. Recently I tried the haemul pajeon (seafood scallion pancakes) and it was SO good, I think they used glutinous flour so it was a bit chewy like mochi, and ultra crispy and light. Kimchi Jjigae was pretty good too, definitely has a spicy kick (5/10 on the spice scale). I've even tried the vegetable bbq platter, which was a great mix of mushrooms, eggplant, peppers, onions, but it was a little heavy on the sesame oil. 

Must orders: fried chicken, tteokbokki rice cakes, dolsot bibimbap with bulgogi, haemul pajeon. BBQ really depends on what cuts you like, but most of them are not marinated (only bulgogi and kalbi are). The weakest part of the menu seems to be the stews, which I prefer to go to Ktown in Manhattan for my fix of budaejiggae and soondubu.
Great service and the bulgogi was amazing.  Try the local IPA as a nice acompianant to the meal.

You don't come here for a traditional KBBQ - the space is what really shines about Insa. Our party of 13 had a seamless, attentive experience from dining to rowdy karaoke, and if you can indulge on the company dollar, Insa's OK.

The highlights from our order that you might also enjoy:

- gogi mandu, meat dumplings fried to a satisfying crisp 
- yuk hwe, Korean-style beef tartare, and very accessible
- tteokbokki, spicy rice cakes
- insa fried chicken, nice and boneless!

However there are a number of questionable additions and decisions that Insa has made that do not stack up well against the many options for KBBQ + karaoke we have in NYC.

- the approach to cooking the meat is decidedly weird: you wait until every piece of meat on a platter is cooked before it is served
- a terrible, local "Insa" soju at 3x the cost of Cham or Chamiseul
- the 'large format cocktails for 6' are for three persons; this isn't a Pocha 32 watermelon soju
- price! the ingredients and execution simply do not justify it
This place is worth it if just for the crispy fried chicken. Great bar connected to the restaurant for cocktails while you wait. Fun place to have a shared (and delicious) meal with friends.

TL;DR: This is a decent place to get your Korean fix in if you're craving it but there is way better food elsewhere for less.

*** AMBIANCE ***
It's nice! There's also a semi-speakeasy like bar room hidden around the corner that is cute and karaoke rooms in the back. Apparently it can get wild here at night.

*** DRINKS ***
Pretty good!

*** FOOD ***
Was not impressed by the banchan (side dishes). For example, the potato salad was underseasoned and the kimchi tasted really off. The rest of the food is good but not outstanding, given the price. The one thing we had that I would come back for were the cumin-rubbed sweet and spicy pork ribs. 

*** SERVICE ***
Good! Our server actually stopped us from ordering too much, which we appreciated.

Let's be honest here. If you read the reviews, you'll see a trend between the rave reviews and negative reviews. As an Asian American, this place is a bastardized Korean BBQ restaurant. It's the equivalent of those fast food Chinese takeout places to real Chinese food. This place is as Korean as fortune cookies is Chinese. I do not recommend this place if you want real Korean food.

You won't be grilling/bbq-ing your own meats here. The portions are tiny and waiters do not understand how to grill. The meats are not browned and there is no flavor except salt. The banchans here are close to disgusting. Usually I love the radish kimchi and here, it tastes like soy sauce. The regular kimchi here is made from lettuce and not cabbage which means it's bitter and nowhere near resembles any type of kimchi. There is no fermentation involved. You can't slap hot pepper flakes and soy sauce on some greens and call it kimchi. Stop insulting Korean food. Before anyone jumps down my throat, I've had non-cabbage kimchi before. I've been served Chinese vegetable kimchi before and it was delicious. I've made my own kimchi before and it was delicious. It's very easy to make. But to make such a bastardized version of kimchi and serve it here is to make it palatable for individuals who are not familiar with Korean flavors. This is the same as the takeout Chinese restaurants. 

The Korean fried chicken here was very disappointing. There is no signature crispy crust that Korean fried chicken usually has. The fried layer is soggy and the sauce is straight up gochujang. Once again, you can't just slap one Korean ingredient on something and call it Korean food. 

For the price, just go to K-town in Manhattan and get real Korean food. Stop being cheated here. You'll be surprised by how real Korean food tastes like and you'll never come back here again.

Rip off BK korean restaurant !
U can have triple quality and cheaper in Ktown.  
The quality, flavor, quantity, service all 0 star. We spend almost $300 include drinks 
Still hungry...

We were seated at a table pretty quickly, despite thinking we'd have about 30 minutes at the bar. Great BBQ, but they won't let you cook your own (liability?) which means everything gets cooked at once and then cools off. Meh. The pancakes were ok, sides were excellent. Overall good but don't need to go back unless I'm with a group and we plan to karaoke.

Fun spot! Staff was friendly. Funky decor at the bar and large space for big groups at the tables. You can come though with just 2 people, their bbq tables adjust to accommodate large and small grounds alike. We ordered the squid and octopus as well as the pork belly for the bbq. The staff cook the proteins for you - you just sit back and watch. Overall, generous portions and the squid / octopus especially was very soft and delicious! They have interesting drinks selection, including several sojus and sakes in addition to cocktails, wine and beer. Definitely want to gov back.

Came here once for dinner with my gf. The bar area had a laid back vibe with great cocktails! Definitely recommend them. 

For dinner the service was pretty mediocre. The server left our vegetables on the grill for such a long time that I myself had to cook them. They were next to us attending a much bigger party and forgot that they placed them on the grill. Once they came back we asked for new vegetables and sent a new server in their place.

Pros

-The bar was cozy and intimate for a date
-Cocktails were complex, interesting and tasty
-Wait for seating wasn't too long

Cons

-Did not feel like authentic Korean bbq
-Dishes ordered didn't match description
-Service lacked attention to detail

As someone who doesn't write Yelp reviews very often, I had to come on here to recommend against coming here if you wanted a Korean BBQ fix. However, I can say that my server was wonderful. He would check up on our table even though he had other tables to take care of and when he was busy he made sure someone else was grilling our meat for us. That being said, my experience with the food here was subpar.

As someone who LOVES Korean food and Korean bbq ,everything here was pretty much a complete disappointment. The seafood pancake we had barely had any seafood in it, it was pretty much just batter and scallions and rather burnt as well. The pork belly was not the usual thick cuts I'm used to at places like Jongro, Kang Ho Dong, etc. and looked pretty much like what your average piece of bacon would look like. To make it worse the 3 pathetic slices we were given cost $29! Absolutely absurd.

The beef brisket was nothing special and the quality of it barely seemed better then any AYCE bbq place. The kalbi was the star of the dinner because the marinade made it taste a lot better then the other meats we had, but again would be lackluster compared to any of my regular korean bbq joints. 

Overall, I will not be returning. High prices for a quantity and quality of meat that does not match the cost, there are better options elsewhere.
Great Atmosphere! Enjoyed the Dolsat Bi Bim Bap! Be advised they add a 20% gratuity regardless of the size of your party

Everything is SALTY.

The meat, the side dishes, even the drinks...ok maybe not the drinks cuz we got water and soju, but you get the idea.

Service was also slow, had to call for our server several times for refills on side dishes as well as ask for our remaining meat dish....which seems like it as sitting on the counter for a while.

Atmosphere/setting: I do like the bench seats and table set up but the ventilation system sucks.

A very "American" Korean bbq place. 

Gets 2 stars instead of 1 because we did have a great karaoke experience.

Bottom line: Korean bb-quit

This place is pretty amazing. My wife and I enjoyed Insa several times before we were married. The food was great, and the service was always great. When it came to finding a venue when we decided on a date for our wedding, Insa immediately came to mind.

We reached out, and got a super reasonable quote. Jamie, the General Manager, worked with us on everything from the menu to the event planning. What could have been a stressful thing turned out to be a breeze. During the event, the staff couldn't have been more attentive and accommodating. The whole experience was really great.

This review is for our server Lexie. After reading reviews, we were skeptical about going because it said the service was bad. However, our server LEXIE was AMAZING! Not only was she super friendly with great recommendations, she actually hand wrote us a detailed list of places to check out in Philly for our upcoming trip. 5 stars for Lexie! Additionally, the food was incredible.

This is my favorite karaoke spot in NYC now that Pulse is closing. It's only $60 for 2 hours in a private room, so if you have a big group it's really cheap, and there's no minimum order for drinks. The song selection is decent, the controls are intuitive, and the bathrooms are clean, numerous, and easy to find.

There's an adjoining restaurant that I must admit I've never actually eaten at, although my Korean housemate tells me the Korean BBQ there is solid. Also, there's a comfortable bar with nice cocktails where you can wait if you're not ready to get a room yet.

The service has always been great here and they have good prices and good product. I'm actually rather surprised the place isn't more crowded. Perhaps I've just never been there at peak traffic.

Went here Friday night with a large group. The interior is stunning, the bar being an absolute work of art. Wait staff was very helpful, basically told us what to order. The beef is exceptional and everything else was very good as well. Had some friends who stopped by, weren't gonna stay for dinner but the teen kids starting devouring the food once it was laid to table. So did everyone else. The included gratuity made paying straight forward. Imagine is useful in a restaurant catering to large parties. We went to a karaoke room afterwards. They brought a dessert and candle to my 14 year old kid at midnight on her birthday. Was perfect.

Came here on a Sunday night with a party of 5 and there was no wait. The interior had a really clean and modern vibe, very casual atmosphere. 

Shortly upon ordering our food, the banchans came. There is only one way to tell whether or not a Korean restaurant is solid: their kimchi. And unfortunately, the kimchi was really bland. We ordered a whole Insa Fried Chicken, there were some boneless pieces, as well as whole drumsticks and wings. It was a good, thin crisp however the sauce was really salty. For the entree I had the Seollongtang which had a rich, creamy broth. Mild so you can season it to your liking. A generous amount of meat and tendon, loved it. We also ordered the Soondae appetizer but it came after all our entrees. I've never had soondae before so I can't compare. But it didn't taste like anything, just a mushy texture. 

Overall a chill atmosphere, I loved the seollongtang but the other dishes I had weren't really impressive. Staff were attentive and our waiter made sure to keep checking up on us

Delicious Korean BBQ! They don't take reservations for parties less than 6, so I waited about an hour on a Friday night - very well worth it. I ordered the kkot deungshim (28 day dry aged ribeye) and bolsal (pork jowl). If you like buttery, fatty cuts, I highly recommend the bolsal. The items from the BBQ menu come with the traditional side dishes like kimchi and daikon, to name a few. They actually give you brown rice, instead of white, which I don't normally have with my KBBQ, but it complemented the meat very well. The meat was so juicy and flavorful with the perfect amount of that good grilled taste. I also appreciate the staff cooking the meat for us because sometimes I'm just too lazy to cook my own KBBQ. I'll definitely be coming back!
Very fun atmosphere and food is good.  Prices seem high because gratuity is included.  The challenge for me is I always forget and add 20% tip making my meal 40% more expensive.

I squirmed in my seat the entire meal. The inauthenticity of the food prep, wait staff, and environment as a whole was uncomfortable and disappointing. In general the flavors were okay but the rice in the bibimbap was sub par and items were generally over-priced. If you want Korean BBQ, go to Manhattan. I won't make the same mistake again!

I have a question: does this restaurant always add 20% tip to your bill? I mean, I always tip more than 20% so it's not a problem for me but just curious if I'm the only one got this *special* treatment or not (we were a party of three.)

Review: food is good. Not too special for the price.

So I have to say I was impressed here.  I am not familiar with Korean cuisine so I asked our waiter "Wilson" for some recommendations.  We had "Gogi Mandu" steamed dumplings that were outstanding, "Yangnyum Galbi" short ribs that Trini grilled right in front of us and melted in my mouth, "Japchae" sweet potato noodles were amazing. There were small sides I wish I could remember the names but were awesome and I loved the kick they had.  Looking forward to coming again.

The food is overpriced for what you actually get and the service sucks. They add a 20% "admin fee" to the bill which is fine, I usually always tip 20% anyway but this did not deserve that much. The karaoke rooms looked fun but I wouldn't be hurrying back

Recently visited Insa for an group dinner with about 12 people. Was able to make a somewhat last minute reservation for an early dinner slot.

The food was good but overall I would say a bit too pricey. We ordered a ton of appetizers and plates and got 4 different orders of the bbq (beef short rib, ribeye, squid/octopus etc. some of the standouts were the seafood pancake, sweet potato japchae and the dumplings. The meat was good but not mind blowing 

The service was generally okay but one of our waitresses was a bit rude and short with us :( this was pretty unfortunately given we were celebrating a birthday and her attitude was rude and made people feel uncomfortable. I get that big groups are tricky, but you should be prepared to offer great service to all party sizes

Great atmosphere and staff! Wait was a bit longer than expected but the hostess provided us free drinks for the inconvenience which was really nice. 

One thing to note, there's an automatic 20% gratuity added regardless of the size of your party. 

The food was good as well nothing extremely memorable but a good experience nonetheless. We weren't particular fans of the drinks but they have a decent cocktail selection.

This isn't Korean food. It isn't even fusion. I came here so excited to find Korean food nearby but now I know why I never heard of this place. It isn't even *good* food. Don't let the pretty presentation, chill ambience, or fancy prices fool you. Food gets worse with each bite. Kimchi tasted brined instead of fermented. Dude WTF was that deep fried tteok and potato chips in bbq sauce doing calling itself tteokbokki? And for $17? Also the bibimbap is heavy and oily, wrong type of rice, wrong oil, bulgogi tasted like chinese beef w/broccoli, and even the whole dish of kochujang couldn't save it. I'd be shocked if a single Korean person was involved in this establishment, I can see the headline, Random American Who Has Never Eaten Korean food Opens Restaurant. It's a travesty. I am sad. The crowd in here is neither Asian nor discerning Park Slope foodie because both know better. Now I do too. I am so disappointed, I came here so excited to eat Korean food after getting a craving for tteokbokki... And sadly my craving still isn't sated. If you want good Korean food, hop the N/R or F or any train from Atlantic and get yourself to 32nd st. Even the worst food in ktown is worth the 30 min trip over this! Your wallet and taste buds will thank you.

Insa, please hire a Korean to fix this mess. Your location, staff, and presentation are decent, please make the food match up so I can be as excited about this place as I was before I was served!

Least favorite Korean restaurant! The food was expensive and didn't taste authentic, like it was missing the traditional touches of Korean culture. Don't let the presentation of the dishes fool you. The restaurant has a great vibe but the food is inferior to any other Korean restaurant in NY. Stick to K-Town if you want good affordable Korean dishes. We ordered tteokbokki and got something that was somewhat inspired by tteokbokki, not what we expected at all- they should have called it something different because what we ate was not tteokbokki! The dolsot bibimbap with bulgogi was oily and missing key flavors that makes true bibimbap delicious. The bibimbap was very mediocre and not spicy or saucy enough. If the owners are Korean I would be very shocked and appalled because it's a travesty and how poor the quality of food is here. Very disappointed with the food experience! I won't be coming back again.

This was my first Korean BBQ experience...and I really enjoyed it! The cafeteria style wooden benches and dim lighting were very modern and cute. Our server was very sweet and she made some recommendations since it was our first time eating Korean BBQ.  Overall, it was a little bit pricey but I knew that before going in so it wasn't an issue. 

We got here at 6pm on a Tuesday and it was completely empty. By 7pm, the after work crowd had arrived and the place was packed. If we had come at 7pm, we definitely would have had to wait, so you may want to make a reservation if you're planning to come after 7pm. Also- There are karaoke rooms in the back and it was pretty lively for a Tuesday night. The karaoke prices are so reasonable that I want to come back just for that... everyone looked like they were having a great time.

This place is the best I had one of the best cooks he cooked all our food to perfection he was kind enough to make sure our big table of 20 all got some of the bbq he also was grilling on both ends of the table witch was impressive this place is deff a repeat only con they have a 20% admin fee witch I don't think goes to our cook so I decided to tip him extra on the side

Insa is one of my neighborhood go-tos. I'm vegetarian, and my partner is vegan, and their bibimbap with tofu (egg optional!) is great. The cocktails are good and the vibe is nice, especially on the later end when it's a bit more quiet.

I came here on a Saturday night with a group of 8 to celebrate a birthday and we all had a great time.  We arrived around 7:30 and waited about an hour and fifteen minutes to be seated.  We waited in the bar, which was fine, but it does get super crowded.  One thing that was a bit off-putting, as others have mentioned, was the 20% administrative fee.  I understand this for food service, but I ordered one glass of wine ($13) and the service fee was $2.70.  Maybe there should be a drink minimum to charge the service fee at the bar..?  However, once we were seated, all of the food was very delicious - my favorite was the japchae.  I was with two friends who lived in South Korea for about 4 years and they said all the food seemed to taste very authentic.

First of all, this is a decent place, spacious room with great decorations. However, the food..to be honest, it is not worth the money at all. I have tried a lot different Korean BBQ restaurants, most of them taste better than this one with more reasonable price. The short rib was not bad, but with the money I spent, I was expecting more. Also the 20% administration fees on my bill surprised me‍‍. This was my first time here, and would be my last time eating here.

No seafood in seafood pancake. Don't order seafood pancake. My pork belly was burned, tasted very bitter. My friend asked the waitress which part of cow is beef brisket from. She goes like: I don't eat meat. Do you have a smart phone? Other than that, meat was decent and mushroom was delicious!

I had a late meal there and it doesn't taste like Korean food. They used too much oils I think. And they just put some burned stuff in the dish. It's actually expensive there and tastes not good at all. I won't go to this restaurant next time for sure.

Love the gap between the outside vs inside! Came here on a Saturday night around 6:30pm (unplanned) and the place is packed. We were told it was going to be around an hour and a half wait so we trotted over to the bar area. 

After lingering and preying on seats, we finally were able to snatch a table. Score! 

(I don't remember the actual dish names, sorry in advance!) We got the fried chicken (half order), kimchi pancake, pork belly and spam bibimbap. This was for 3 people.lol. There was more than plenty. 

All the dishes were delicious. No complaint. From all that we ordered, I would say get the pork belly. It was delicious! And the pancake. 

But just keep in mind, prices aren't cheap. A lot people are writing that they could find places in K-Town that are cheaper. Well, yeah...duh. 

Every staff member was nice as well. 

If you want to karaoke, make sure to call beforehand to reserve a time slot. By 8pm, all time slots were full for the night.
Great for family style with friends! And karaoke in the back.  The service was great and the atmosphere was top notch!

I really liked the food (korean BBQ and dolsot bibimbap) and staffs were really welcoming and kind. Yet, I need to point out that I saw the dirt on vegetables (ssam) for BBQ and I can't avoid thinking that I must have eaten some of them. When I closely look at the vegetables, they weren't fresh either....
Excellent food and customer service... actually taste authentic... recommend bim bop... food has great flavor...

Yelp so kindly erased my review of Insa 3 years ago, so I will keep my rewrite brief. 

Insa is a welcome oasis in the the giant Korean desert that South Brooklyn is. Sure more options have creeped up over the years but short of a cab ride to KTown you are not going to find more authentic and just plain satisfying Korean food than Insa. And there is certainly no other places in miles where you will find a dedicated banchan chef (these are the small insanely delicious little samples of food they give you when you sit down). 

Again since I already used up part of my life writing this review, I will cut to chase. 

Skip the traditional BBQ here (go to a place with real charcoal instead) and go straight to the Budae Jjigae (army base spam stew). It is truly one the best dishes I have had anywhere. Just the perfect combo of spicy heartiness that warms yours soul. For some idiotic reason they don't show on menu anymore but if you ask nicely they will make. 

While I realize Bibimbop is the pad Thai of Korean food they do a phenomenal job of it here. 

The cocktails and beer selection is always just right here and the service impeccable. Tip is included which makes group outings so much easier.

This review is mainly for the karaoke. The karaoke room was nice and clean, but SO overpriced! We were in the big room (couldn't downsize) and ended up paying ~$800 for 3 hours of singing and a couple of pitchers of beer. They bill it as $160/hr but with tax and fixed 20% gratuity, it gets expensive quickly. You can get better deals elsewhere. I won't be singing here again...

The restaurant was delicious. Get the kalbi and grilled mushrooms.

have been here several times for dinner. we always have fun. the food is good and the scorpion bowls even better. my friends and i go and have a nice meal and several scorpion bowls. you can't go wrong with that! the staff is friendly. the bar that is in the front is cool. decorated quirky and nice mood lighting.

Service was really slow and at the end of my meal they took my tea away before I even finished half of it. So much for included gratuity.... They need it be more on top of their service if they are going to include a service fee.

This review is for the bar only...very rude bartender. I have never felt so unwelcomed by another woman. Dismissive and patronizing to me; kind and warm to my male partner. The first time it happened I wrote it off as minor - she's probably got a lot going on - like all of us. But on a second visit, six months later - same bartender, same treatment. That's fine - there's lots of places to go in Brooklyn.

The food is wonderful and staff in the restaurant incredibly helpful and generous.
The best soondaeboo around. Better than ktown in either flushing or Manhattans ktown. No msg either!

This place is definitely over priced for its food. The meat was cooked okay but all the veggies were burned and tasted bitter and dry. Definitely not coming back. Most of the food was way too salty as well. There were way too many staff just standing around and only half of the tables were occupied on a Friday night.

Insa was good... but I'm always looking for the authentic Korean experience so the atmosphere was a little bougie. Ordered kalbi, soon du bu (soup) and the pork belly. All tasted good, but not sure I need to go back compared to all the options in k town. I would go back, however, for the karaoke with friends!

This is the worst "Korean" BBQ restaurant ever made. Korean is in quotations because there is nothing authentic about the food. Doesn't seem like they understand the cuisine and everything is overpriced for what you get. I'd suggest going to Korea town if you want a real experience. It's a shame too because it all looks new inside and they have other things to offer than just dinner. But you'd probably not want to waste your time and money coming here.

I'm not sure they even deserve 1 star. We were treated with contempt when ask to be seated away from the kitchen, ignored when we tried to order and then served food that was mediocre at best. I'm guessing that no one who works there cares because service is included. This place is one of the worst managed restaurants. What a insult!

Service was excellent! Our waitress was so good we tipped more than the automatic percentage that was applied to our bill. We ordered the short rip & brisket they were so flavorful. The wings are to die for so crispy/crunchy/sweet/a little spicy .. their sauces were on point and the side veggies were fresh and flavorful. We went on Friday lunch time and it was a casual and quiet atmosphere. Definitely returning :)

Let's get the bad out of the way; this place was way too expensive and I do mean way too expensive!!! Don't get me wrong, I walked in with my eyes open- I knew the prices before going. I did not mind the price of the food for the portions served but the 20% service charge in the bar, then another 20% service charge at dinner, then another 20% service charge in the karaoke room which was $60 per hour (we booked for 2 hours)for the room we had two eight ounce cokes and the 20% service charge in the karaoke room came to $25.20! Now get this; the 20% service charge is not a tip and is not directly given to your server. It goes to the owner so that he can pay all employees a decent wage and also provide healthcare. Not fair for customers to have to pay for that. Your receipt comes with no space to leave your server a tip but you feel bad not leaving a tip so you dig in your pocket again and give your server a cash tip, especially after excellent service(They deserve a tip). Okay, now for the good; the service was superior to say the least! The staff was very knowledgeable and courteous. The food was very tasty and portion size was adequate. Overall, we had a great time and I must say that they let you know about the service charge up front if you can read. They don't tell you about it but it is in the menu and on their website.
Price is high, portion is small, quality is mediocre, free side dishes are okay. Much better off going to Korean town near Penn Station or go across the street to Threes Brewing for other cuisine.

Korean food is one of my favorites and I was excited to try a Korean restaurant in BK. Came here for a Friday night dinner and had a good time. In order to be seated make sure your whole group is with you. Just know you can get your name down, but they won't seat you. But don't despair. The bar in the back is the perfect waiting spot to get a drink and wait. Nice selection of wine, cocktails and beer. It did not take long to get a table which was surprising but great. There is a vast option of meats and dishes to choose from. We mostly got meat dishes and one vegetarian dish. You have the option of grilling everything on your own or you can do it yourself. We had someone grill for us and they were very nice, attentive and cooked the food pretty good. At one point the A/C started leaking on a few of us and he moved us to another table and made sure we were comped desert for the trouble. The mix of meats we got were good but honestly not memorable. It might be the fact that, this place, and Korean bbq overall is expensive and with that price tag, you are looking for something amazing! If you are to order anything get the Beosut Modeum (mushroom platter) and the Ojingeo & Nakji (squid and octopus). Highly recommend. We got three other meats that were honestly not memorable for me. The service was great, and they always made sure the table was filled with sides and lettuce. From their drink menu, get the Mai Tai. If you are into tiki drinks, this is a must. If I come back, lets just say it will be for this drink. Overall, I had a good time, and the food was good but was it worth the dent it put in my wallet....no.

Wasn't bad but I thought it was over priced. The meats were relatively small portioned and staff seemed unfamiliar with the process of the KBBQ (its cool though, I think they were new). Highlight was definitely the dry age beef, that was excellent. I also tried the blood sausage and panchetta which were both okay, but for the price I was hoping for either more in flavor or more in quantity. 

They have a full kitchen, so maybe next time it'd be best to stick to the prepared food vs. the kbbq.

This was chosen by me and group of work friends for a down town after work one night to blow off steam of the stressful day. It was a fun easygoing night had by all. The staff was courteous, the service was above par and excellent. The Karaoke rooms were not messy, the staff works hard to keep them really clean and sanitary and it shows  - it was clean and it was a just really great place that we could hang out for a little while and laugh.

 

The food was delicious - I would definitely recommend the Banchan, Fried Chicken and the Marinated short ribs. Yes, this can get pricey because you are having a good time and you are enjoying happy hour so I am not going to lie - it is going to be a night out to spend out, but for a great night out for with great people every so often. It is a fantastic escape from work stress place that I highly recommend will definitely be back again keep my karaoke room ready

The food and service was outstanding, great location and great space.

Staff was extremely friendly and fun, overall an excellent experience.

I just finished eating there and the food is very, very good, a bit of complexity in the flavor combos but no heat, all around zing and pop but no bite and ouch, meaning absolutely perfect for me. IThe very best corn dog ever! But the service was not what it should be, it took forever to get a glass of water and they do the thing of grabbing your plate when you are not done and then the cocktails came out way after the food. Still it was very tasty and it's a fun atmosphere.

This place was highly underwhelming. If you want good Korean BBQ, go to Koreatown, and literally any random place will be better. They obviously don't know much about Korean food. The beef (we had short ribs and brisket) is fatty, the cuts are not well considered, and the banchan (little dishes) are insufficient -- a real Korean restaurant floods the table with options. The service is spotty -- and why would they bother doing any better when the "administrative fee" is already added in lieu of tipping. And after all that, the prices are high -- it's actually quite expensive. What a disappointment! I had been looking forward to trying this place, but I most definitely won't go back.

As a visitor to the city I would have had no idea this place was here. It feels hidden in an alley with only a wooden door and illuminated beer sign to leaf the way. Fantastic food and if you feel like celebrating, rent a personal karaoke room

This review is strictly for the karaoke and bar area. Originally my friends and I came here 8pm for karaoke. But they were booked until 11:30pm. We thought about going somewhere else but the only other karaoke place we can think of in Brooklyn was in sunset area. Luckily, 20 minutes later, we were told that there was a cancellation for 9:30pm. So my friends and I sat down at the bar for appetizers and drinks. The drinks and food were reasonable priced. An hour later, we were escorted to one of the karaoke rooms. They have 5 rooms towards the back of the restaurant. What I love about this place is the price. I'm so used to doing karaoke in Ktown, the price for this place was fresh of breath air. For 10 people, it was a flat rate of $60 per hour. We stayed two hours which was $15 after tip and tax for each person. There was a button in the room that you press whenever you need a servant. They only had English songs but the music was up-to-date. All the servants were friendly and attentive.

My first thought stepping into Insa... "TOTO, we are definitely not in Ktown"

It's located on a side street lined with business storage but once you step inside it's a wide open space with picnic tables set up. Came here on a Thursday at 5:30pm and of course I asked if they have any happy hour specials. It's $2 off draft beers and wine. It's not much considering it's $8 for beer and $10 for wine.

We ordered a mix of BBQ with a stew and some dish (for the table) to share.
Galbi ($36) - marinated short ribs - this was quite tasty but my god the portion is small. We had 4 girls but I felt like I could have eaten the whole thing myself.

Samgyeopsal ($28) - thick sliced pork belly - ok clearly false advertising or they need to get a new supplier because it looked like regular oscar mayer bacon and I'm not talking about the thick cut either. Also, WAYYYYY too salty. If you have high blood pressure, stay away from this dish.

Insa Fried Chicken (half $18) - this was just ok. I've honestly had better. The meat was dry unless you just eat the drumstick. My friend got the drumstick and she said it wasn't dry but still nothing to be oohing and ahhing about. 

Tteokbokki ($17) - Spicy Rice Cakes, Fish Cakes, Soft Boiled Egg - this was by far the best dish we had there. The rice cake is slightly deep fried so it has a crispy texture and the flavor was good. Only con is again portion size. 

Soondubu* ($16) - Spicy Silken Tofu Stew with Shellfish - again, just ok. Nothing special and it wasn't even that spicy. Trust me, I can only handle mild spice so the fact that I finish my bowl of soup means there was barely any heat to it. Was it good? Honestly I can't remember, that's how unmemorable this dish was.

Good to Know: They don't have a tipping system but they DO have 20% administrative fee. I don't know what that actually means but our server was really attentive and grilled all our food to perfection. So I hope that 20% does benefit our server in some ways and not end up in the owner's pocket.

So overall, I don't think this place is worth a repeat. With the high price attached to small portions and just 1 memorable dish,  this is not worth the recommendation. So next time you're in the mood for some Korean BBQ, hop on a train and head to ktown!

This review is solely based on my experience with the bartender at Insa (5/19/17). As soon as my friends and I walked at the bar and took our seats the short female bartender treated us with hostility. Sometimes you can sense it. First I thought it was only me. I asked my friends and they felt the same. I have no idea why and we are still baffled. We didn't do anything but treat her with respect. In my 17 years in the NYC I have never felt so uncomfortable at a bar. If the manager is reading this it is important to address that the first experience makes a lasting impression. Although kudos to the other bartender who at least smiled and didn't throw the menu at our faces like bricks. I understand the neighborhood demographic is changing. But you should expect clients from all walks of life. All the customers should be treated with the same level of  respect. Well I'm willing to give the place another try but definitely avoiding the hostile bar area! I'm really hoping that the manager reads this and educates his employees. I have been to many bars in K-town and they offer excellent service. If you are running a Korean establishment how about we embrace those values of courtesy and respect ?

First of all they took a long time to bring the meat to the table. Second of all i think it would've been nice if the waitress would've told me that the fried rice was spicy. What if I was allergic to spices ? 
I been other Japanese restaurants so I have an idea of how the food is.

My girlfriend and I have been coming here for the past year or so and love it.  We used to go to Moim for our neighborhood Korean fix -  another Park Slope restaurant that closed.  The girlfriend lived in Korea for 6 years and describes it as a mix of some classic korean dishes and some contemporary.  I think it's all really good.  Also great they have authentic BBQ at the tables and give you the choice of doing it yourself and having the wait staff help.  Haven't tried the karaoke spots but they look like fun.  Nice open space.  Great cocktails though we pretty much stick now to Tiger's Eye when we visit.  Haven't had anything I didn't like.  Usually get the BBQ meats and start with the seafood pancake.  We also once had some kind of fried calamari, which we great and unique tasting, but it wasn't on the menu the last time we were there.  My only complaint is they are a little on the pricey side, though we can't help but over order whenever we go.

Went here while visiting my daughter. We went with several of her friends after a training session at her gym just a couple doors down.  Someone else ordered for the group - but he made good choices. Appetizers we're good - my personal fave was black beans. And Sake. 
The main course were larger bowls with meat or tofu and rice and veggies. Very good. 
The food was good and we had a blast sitting around the table!
Went recently for a b'day dinner. Ambiance was good. Staff was pleasant. Karaoke was fun! Not enough food.

This is actually the first Korean restaurant I've loved! Every dish was scrumptious...here is the order, Fried chicken, lamb chops,  seafood and scallion pancakes, japchae, dumplings, stir fry squid with udon noodles, short ribs. It was a bit pricey but worth it!

A standout of this restaurant is the exceptionally rude waitstaff who were uncooperative about seating and enquiries about seating. We waited for over an hour and we were not pushy just asked a few times about time estimate. And they still deliberately dragged out changing over seats etc and was hostile and condescending in attitude. As the restaurant had a mandatory 20% service surcharge they must feel they can act how they want and ignore their customers as they feel like. Of course this is one of the only times where I've actually really wanted to cut the tip - but couldn't. The food is fine - to standard Korean probably a bit on the pricey side and not as much choice or authenticity compared to Ktown counterparts - nothing out if the ordinary that would justify or go anyway towards offsetting f the poor attitude. The drinks list is quite light on actual Korean alcohol which is surprising considering how many good beers and other alcoholic drinks Korea is known for. I have had much better food and value and authentic experience in k town. Will not be going back.

Went here for a work dinner. The K-Town was my drink of choice all night. The highlights were the pork belly and the short rib. The grilled mushrooms were also a nice touch.

The fried chicken was ok. Wasn't a big fan of the bibimbap either. 

I'd come here again since it's near my home. Service was good.

The dining room here is LOUD. Overwhelmingly loud.

Highlights were the seafood scallion pancake and the BBQ beef short ribs - everything else was just ok, and over all it's expensive for what you get.

Karaoke was way better than dinner - good group cocktails, and reasonable room rates.
This place is amazing. Beautifully-built, incredible ambience, great food. Brunch is my favorite time to go.
Love the food, love the vibe. Make a reservation if you want a table, or be prepared to wait. The bar is great. And they were super nice in the bar about making me a drink without cane sugar.

I hate to have to leave a negative review, but this place is just not cutting it. The ambiance is pleasant enough, but the food is subpar and it just doesn't give off that authentic Korean vibe to me. I'm use to chatting it up with the ahjumma's and ahjussi's, but I didn't get that here. It was way too gentrified; to the point where you can tell just by the food. I'm a big foodie, so I was very disappointed. You live and you learn though.

I've had the pleasure of hanging out at Insa twice now. The first time was for a company party in which all of the food and karaoke was paid for. My second visit was with a group of friends and all I could remember was "wow $$$". This place can get to be kind of expensive but in the end both of my experiences were unforgettable. 

The important highlights for me are the fried chicken is amazing! So good that I plan on just sitting at the bar soon and ordered fried chicken. The drinks were strong! I can't give the specifics of the drinks I ordered but I did have an epic hangover the next day. The place was super crowded on a Friday evening but that made for a very fun vibe. The karaoke is fun! You get a private room. There are small  rooms for smaller groups and a larger room that can fit a larger group of people. 

On both of my visits I've never had a problem with the service. The server have been knowledgeable, youthful, and kind. Overall, I'll definitely be back would recommend it to others.

We were charged a 20% fee notated as an administration fee to provide a living wage. But it's not a gratuity.  I'm confused- I'm paying an administrative fee and helping provide a living wage but I don't work here.  If you want your staff to have a living wage, please lay it yourself.  That's not my responsibility.  Not a good business practice.

We went with a large group.  The food was awesome.  If you go on the early side for dinner it's very kid friendly.  Friendly and knowledgable service.  Good vibe and beautiful space.  Good ventilation.  Karaoke is lots of fun too.  I highly recommend Insa.
Very good food - pricing is a bit on the pricey end. Will check out the karaoke rooms next visit.

Called at 6pm to see if they had tables available in 30 minutes, they said definitely. Got there 6:30 and there was an hour wait and the host had zero sense of apology. Did not try the food or drink but bad first impression. Had a great Korean dinner in prospect heights instead.

It was a tough call for me to give this place 3-stars. 

1. I'm not a fan of Korean BBQ places - I came here with a group so please consider that. 
2. 5-star ratings for me are reserved for places that are the BEST at what they do and I like. 
3. 4-star ratings are reserved for places I really like but aren't the best...

So a 3-star rating is as best as this can get. 

The food is pretty much Korean BBQ... I'd suggest the ribeye... which is pretty much the only thing I liked... the beef bisque I would ask them to cook it longer (again, personal preference) ... outside of that if you're coming to a Korean BBQ you are probably coming bc you like it - and the people I was with spoke highly of it. 

Now, for what I can speak on... the ambiance. Noise level is high and it is a somewhat cafeteria seating which adds to it. Kereokee (sp?) in the back and people seem to be having a good time at it. 

Only had my Diet Coke refilled one time ... and the guy who refilled it wasn't our service guy... would have liked to have more consistent service throughout the entire meal - at the beginning I felt like an Emperor!
Having such authentic Korean food in Brooklyn is amazing. Even better when it is made by Chef Sohui! Her flavors are outstanding! It's a must visit!!
Had a horrific experience with one of the bartenders at Insa this past Friday night. Nice space, but I will not be returning (nor will the ~15 others I was with).

Trendy hip Korean BBQ. Creative menu, good food, and fantastic service. Shout out to the lovely Rah-Nee and the charming Eddie. They made this weary, hungry business traveler feel welcome. 

However, they didn't get a fifth star because the business owners charge you 20% of your bill to help pay the staff and provide benefits. And here I thought the actual EMPLOYER was supposed to do that.

good food and atmosphere . But let me get this straight Insa owners, you do not offer table service in part of your restaurant - which means we have to get up from our table to order at the bar. Yet... you automatically add on 20 % gratuity to the bill with the usual corporate "in order to ensure the wellbeing of our staff, etc"? tell you what . Pay your staff well first of all. Second , don't force me to give a 20 percent tip when I have to get up and order my food . If you dont offer table service , why are you charging full gratuity for your staff?

KenScale: 3.0/10

The moment I saw the menu where there was marinated galbi (short ribs) but not the non-marinated one, I immediately knew there was something wrong with Insa. Typically, galbi is marinated when the kitchen lacks confidence in the quality of the meat. Yes, marinated one tastes sweeter but really the right way to eat galbi is in its non-marinated form without seasoning to give maximal effect to the meat's texture. After a rather underwhelming dinner at a "modern Korean" restaurant Atoboy the other night, my girlfriend and I (both from Korean background) wanted to make it up by having a more traditional Korean experience focusing on grilled meat. It's pretty rare to see a Korean restaurant in Brooklyn compared to Manhattan (around Korea Town in midtown) or Queens (in the Flushing neighborhood), and I was certainly intrigued to visit Insa located in the quiet neighborhood of Gowanus, especially after a favorable review in NYTimes' restaurant critic Pete Wells. After the meal, I had to keep wondering whether Mr. Wells was probably too drunk from all the sojus and wild night at the karaoke that's inside the restaurant. I really hate to slam a Korean restaurant, but Insa was by far one of the worst dining experiences ever since I came to New York City five years ago. My girlfriend and I are not picky eaters at all, but we were both eager to walk out of the restaurant as soon as the bill came.

Insa is billed as a Korean BBQ restaurant showcasing the traditional Korean barbecue and other dishes. Knowing that the restaurant was from a couple one of whom is from Korea, I was hoping that the kitchen can deliver that satisfying authentic Korean experience. Not only did the kitchen fail to do that, but the food was just plain bad. The beef tartare dish ("yuk hwe") is supposed to have layers of chewy texture, but the one from Insa was just a pile of amorphous meat with no textural effect at all. There wasn't enough pear to add that refreshing kick to the dish, and the egg yolk further dulled the texture without enhancing it. My girlfriend and I looked at each other immediately as if we had seen a ghost after the first scoop. The textural disaster also took over blood sausage ("soondae"). Again, instead of layers of chewy texture that we were expecting, it turned out to be so mushy that I had to try a couple more pieces just to make sure that I was eating what they claim it is. I was absolutely incredulous that Mr. Wells in NYTimes praised this dish with enthusiasm in his review. After the initial shock from finding out there wasn't a non-marinated galbi, we relented and ordered the marinated one, and the texture of galbi was uneven to say the least (the very next day, as a sign of my apology to my girlfriend for a terrible dinner, I took her to an above-average Korean BBQ place in Korea Town where we indulged on juicy, tender galbi in its non-marinated form). The only marginally decent dish to me was the bibimbap rice dish in a stone bowl accompanied by bulgogi, gochujang sauce and fried egg (even though my girlfriend didn't approve this dish either), but there arises another major issue at Insa. In Korean traditional experience, a rice dish comes after all the appetizers and barbecue dishes, and the server brought out the bibimbap at the very beginning! When I stepped into Insa, I didn't see a single Korean server, and it clearly shows that the service staff at this purportedly Korean restaurant doesn't have a clue on how Korean food should be eaten. And for that, the restaurant charges 20% automatic service charges (instead of traditional tips that can be given by diners at their discretion)? Give me a break! 

The restaurant was moderately packed in the course of our dinner with mostly local Brooklynites. Another bad miscue from the restaurant; they only serve natural wines which are not best eaten with the grilled Korean barbecue dishes. Enough said about the lack of common sense from the service staff as noted above. It was really had to find any redeeming qualities from our disastrous dinner at Insa. Two major lessons learned: (1) Mr. Wells doesn't know what Korean food is supposed to taste like and (2) always be wary of a Korean restaurant in a neighborhood that doesn't cater to Korean customers. I've recently put a lot of time thinking about how to write this review. I don't meant to sound mean or hurtful when talking about sub-par dining experience, but I hope that other discerning diners who appreciate the taste of my mother country stay away from this place, until at least they decide to fix their issues (which seems like a pretty tall order to me given the totality of disaster everywhere).

I came here with a party of 8 and a toddler. And no, Dominic I'm not referring to you this time LOL! The staff was super accomodating and the food was hot and fresh. I liked that there is a staff member who will tend to the bbq grilling so you can carry on and not worry about burning your dinner. All the food was delicious and the interior is beautiful. This warehouse district is cool and the space is gorgeous.

Service was excellent! We went to lunch at 1 PM on a Sunday. 
Ordered kimchi jigae, soondobu, seafood pancake, and bibimbap. My sister and I felt the kimchi jigae was a bit too salty. But I like how the kimchi was shredded. They give a lot for the bibimbap. 

This location was an old warehouse but renovated to look modern and ambience felt very comfortable. The windows on the roof (skylights) were perfectly placed. Atmosphere was beautiful. 
The place being a warehouse makes it very spacious, great for parties. It has a lounge/bar section in a different part of the restaurant. And it has private karaoke rooms in the back. 

Overall I wouldn't come back for the food but would definitely come for happy hour, or to host a party.

I had perhaps the worst service experience of my life at Insa. I went last night for a late bite. Despite there being fewer than 10 guests in the dining room it took almost 15 minutes for the waitress to come over from the point we sat down. When she did finally come over she just stood there without any kind of greeting. We ordered BBQ for two and the waitress said, "you're not getting anything else?" Despite the menu saying our order was for two people, the waitress said it's really only enough for one. Brilliant. (In fact, we couldn't finish all the food served to us.) My date and I were taken aback by the attitude in the waitress's voice and she left the table in a minor huff. From that point on we were persona non grata to the waitress. She never checked on us during the meal and was extremely rude when bringing the check, placing the check, and then our credit cards, on the grill surface! When I asked what the 20% admin fee was about, she said "it's so I can actually make a living wage," as if I were some out of touch aristocrat who just ran my carriage over her dog. 

I told the manager what happened, and though he was decently friendly and said "sorry," he didn't seem to take our complaints all that seriously. I understand a manager backing up a member of the staff, but we were guests in their establishment with a serious complaint. He also mentioned that the waitress had mentioned to him that our table was a problem!! Everyone knows wait staff make comments about guests behind closed doors, but for gods sake don't tell the guests about it! This is the only time I've ever complained to a manager about poor service. 

I agree with other reviewers that the 20% admin fee feels dirty when the check comes. Just from a marketing perspective, I think when most people see "admin fee" they immediately think "bullshit surcharge." I'm all for waiters making a living wage. However this was a rare situation where I wish I could have tipped way less than 20%.

The second star is for the (overpriced) food that was actually pretty tasty.
Great atmosphere & food but on the pricey side. Still, the meat was good and you get what you pay for! Bar scene looked fun and I'm definitely checking out renting a karaoke room.
Fantastic Korean BBQ in Brooklyn. Delicious dumplings&a fun atmosphere. Try the cocktail bowl, you won't regret it.

Tried this place a while back and I think I'm going to go back when I'm in Brooklyn in December. The duck, the steamed dumplings or the soup is made with precise detail and time.... Ok it's just damn good!
Came here for a group outing. Great concept for Brooklyn but very expensive for the time spent. Make the whole experience not worth it at all.

Service was excellent BUT.... The food was way below par. As a Korean-American who grew up eating Korean food, I spend a lot of time in the Ktown on 32nd street. I k ow good Korean food. I know how to cook it, and I know how it should taste. There was so much hype about Insa online that I wanted to give it a try. Every single dish we ordered felt like it was missing an ingredient. The kimchijigae had a faint taste of ketchup, and the japchae tasted weirdly of jjajangmyun, which is a Korean/Chinese dish that isn't even served here. We also ordered two servings of samgyupsal, one of which the waitress BURNED while cooking it for us on our table grill. She didn't seem to care and continued, until I finally asked her to lower the heat. She looked surprised and then did so. I just want people to know ahead of time that the food here LOOKS authentic but doesn't TASTE authentic. Also there isn't a single Korean, let alone Asian person on staff, so that should've been the red flag!

I love Insa....especially for karaoke.  I essentially stalked them for months before they opened.  I've eaten there and liked it, but since I think their karaoke outshines their food, I'm going to review that instead.

I've been waiting so so long for a Korean karaoke spot in Brooklyn and this place is the best.  So clean, great songs, and the staff is really nice and actually seem to enjoy working there.  There's an app for their song list, so you're never short of books.

It's sometimes tough to get reservations on the weekend, so book early.  And the room is a flat fee per hour instead of per person, which is actually great because, as Korean karaoke enthusiasts can appreciate, it cuts down on end of the night drama and policing people's time in the room.

The seafood scallion pancake was bombdiggity and the banchan was impressive. Definitely get the Corean mole. Rich and very yummy. The cold noodle was pretty blah and had none of the vinegary oomph that you get in K-town. Also, for a Korean joint, short ribs were not impressive. 2nd time here and we tried the brisket last time. That was better but won't satisfy your craving for Korean bbq. Service was not great. Server barely said anything, was hardly present, and wore work out shorts. Which is too bad bc our server the 1st time was awesome. Still, nice to not have to trek to K-town.

Love this place. The bar is beautiful, and the restaurant is nicely designed too. The food is pretty good - not THE best korean I've had in NYC (which would be in korea town), but given the food, environment and awesome service, I'll be coming back often. Also - it's great for groups.

KBBQ at a good price w/ unlimited munchie dishes. Also great service!

[Experience] We went into Insa after an intense experience of bouldering. (By the way, Brooklyn Bouldering is right down the street from Insa.) The KBBQ was beyond our expectation, and the waiter serving us was extremely helpful. Absolutely love the spacious atmosphere and the food!
