[Food] A friend and I shared one BBQ dish, Chadolbaegi (Thinly Sliced Beef Brisket). The meat was fresh and quite sweet. I highly recommend it! It was served with lots of vege wraps, as well as 9 or 10 munchie dishes. The portion of the meat was not huge, but it was enough to feed two hungry girls who just finished some physical exercises. 

[Price] We were very satisfied with what we got for ~$18 we each paid. Also, we looked around and saw that food on others' tables had pretty good size. So overall, I think Insa is actually slightly cheaper than Ktown restaurants.
Spacious, and will lit. Friendly and helpful staff, especially one particular individual by the name of Yunique. They offer additional space for Karaoke. Food is very tasty and drinks are satisfying.

4.5 stars if I could. I hosted my husband's 40th birthday party here this past Saturday afternoon. We went from 1 table of 14 people to 4 tables of 30 people including kids ages 1.5 to 9 years old. Thankfully the restaurant staff was super professional and flexible in accommodating this - it was a bit of a madhouse on our end with people just showing up - it also helped that it was a quiet summer Saturday afternoon in gowanus and they had those tables open regardless.  The food was delicious - we had galbi BBQ, pork jowl BBQ, japchae, seafood pajun pancakes and crispy fried chicken and kimchi fried rice. My guests kept coming up to me to tell me how good the food was and how cool the space was. Our waiters were all great and provided great service. After lunch, we went into the big karaoke room and had an awesome time. People went out to the bar to get drinks when they felt like it but you can also order food and drinks from the room if you wanted. Karaoke was a big hit for the older kids attending the party. We also had the sangri-la bowl - like sangria with soju - yummy!  I would give this place a 5 star if a) the air conditioning was better in both the main space and the karaoke room (now to be fair, on that day, it was 95 degrees out); b) price was maybe 10% - 15% less - food was delicious but for the smaller serving size, I thought it was pricey; c) maybe a matinee discount on the karaoke rooms for off peak hours ESP for customers who eat a full meal in the main restaurant and d) if there was a better explanation for the "20% administration fee" that was added on the receipt. I assumed it was 20% tip but wasn't sure and felt a bit unsettled because I didn't know if I needed to leave add'l money as separate tip on top of my almost $1500 bill which Included the automatic 20% admin fee.  Final note is that I have to commend the host and staff for being really nice and flexible...they really helped me pull off an awesome and memorable 40th bday party - day time karaoke and all!

Tried it twice and did not like the food or drinks either time. Had a bloody mary the first time. Had trouble finishing it, and that's very unusual for me -- with bloody marys and drinks in general. Not sure what was wrong exactly, but it just didn't taste right. We had the bulgogi that time. It wasn't terrible. I'm very familiar with Korean food, both K-Town casual and more upscale menus, and this was not even close to par. Especially not at that price tag.

Second time we came I ordered another cocktail from the specials menu that looked interesting. It was a vodka drink -- can't remember all the ingredients, but it had seaweed as a garnish and sounded savory. I usually like those types of drinks, but again I had trouble drinking it. Couldn't get it down until after my ice had melted a bit.

Then the bossam came out (((shudders))). I took one bite and literally chewed nothing but cold, gelatinous fat for what felt like 5 minutes, and then had to fight with my gag reflex in order to get it down. Probably thinking I was overreacting, my boyfriend tried a piece too and had the exact same reaction. We sent it back, explaining that it was hard, tough, gelatinous, cold, and basically all fat, and we could not eat it. We ordered something else (bibimbop -- also below average, but I was too traumatized to really eat anything else at that point). They happily charged us for both dishes, and then went ahead and included a nice 20% tip for themselves.

Very disappointed! We had a birthday party here and the service was poor. We had to ask several times for refills of beer and flagged down the waiter every time. For a 20% tip you would think the service would be better. I usually tip that much when I don't have to get the waiters attention every time I need something. 

If the food was amazing, I could forgive the service. There were tiny portions of side dishes, two cups of rice for 8 people. It was about $90 for two people and we left hungry. The short ribs were tough and chewy. Shrimp was standard. 

Never coming here again!

My husband and I went here last night for the first time finally at the behest of some friends. Love the ambiance and vibe of the place. At first, I was a little put off and confused about the service, our guy was in a big rush and several other people seemed to be tending to us at the same time and we weren't sure who to order from. Also got asked to order like 3 times in the 1st 10 minutes of sitting down, love the attentiveness, but after explaining that my husband and I hadn't seen each other all week and we were saying hello, expected a little more patience. It's cool. I get it. And then I realized that this was one of the "no tip" restaurants I'd heard about and the service made instantly more sense. 

The food was on point. Do yourselves a favor and get the half of the house chicken to start. It's basically like the best Korean wings you've ever had. Sauce was sweet, spicy, salty and sour, all the 4 flavor points of good Korean food. Had the sweet potato noodles (which looked more like glass noodles, wasn't really sure) and the short rib bbq. Back to the service on this point too, please don't put the meat on the BBQ for us, we weren't ready yet and had to pull it back off :( Granted, I probably should have said something to you while you were doing it, but just ask first!  

Cocktail, was this magical green thing, I can't remember the name of it but it tasted like drinking a watermelon jolly rancher with fun gummy fruits at the bottom. Yum. They also had an unfiltered lager on tap, which was a great pairing with the spicy chicken. 

We'll definitely be back. App, Noodles, BBQ and two drinks each $130. Solid.

I was not impressed with the food.  The only meat that had any real flavor was the bulgolgi.  Also, they had NO DESSERT! What kind of restaurant does not serve dessert?  I love the korean bbq at Dokebi in Williamsburg.
Great, inexpensive, high quality place. Awesome ambiance and atmosphere. Highly recommended. Cant wait to come back.

Very disappointing!!!
I'm sticking with traveling to K-town or my mom's house for Korean food. The food is mediocre and the service is awful! Even more annoying is an automatic 20% "admin fee" added onto the bill! Guess that's why the service sucks since the staff knows they're going to get tipped regardless of service!

No complaint about drinks or food.  Was there a few months ago, and the food was perfectly fine.  

But the establishment is poorly run.  Called five weeks ago to get a karaoke reservation, only to be told that they are fully booked, except for the one room that they hold for same-day reservations, and to call on that day at noon.  So I did exactly that, only to be told the policy changed and that they already pre-booked the room.  I was on the waiting list for the room, and was never contacted about the policy switch.  

And he kept just saying that all he could do was apologize, which does absolutely no good and leaves me and my guests in a lurch.  Thanks, Insa, for being a poorly run business!

Things That Were Said At Insa Karaoke:

-Guys, we're basically Wilson Phillips.
-You're singing Third Eye Blind, you can have whatever you want.
-Fried chicken tastes good. 
-It's not a hypothetical tambourine! Yes!*
-Pajeon tastes good.
-I love your interpretive dances.
-Man, I felt so many feelings to Eve 6. 
-Holy shit, THAT'S the bottle that cost $100?! 375 ml is not a lot of ml. Well, I guess we better order three more of these tiny things.

Things That Were Not Said At Insa Karaoke:

-Well, that was affordable.
-Man, Peter D is so handsome.

Things That Were Undoubtedly Thought At Insa Karaoke:

-Man, Peter D is so handsome. But he should NEVER sing.
-Perhaps four bottles of vodka was excessive, even if they were tiny.
-The Bossam was probably unnecessary too.
-I'm so glad we don't have to go to K-Town for karaoke and KBBQ anymore...but this is entirely too expensive. 

What I'm trying to say here, is that I really like Insa. The food is good, the karaoke rooms are excellent (as was the service, evidenced by her giving anything we wanted while singing Third Eye Blind), and if you bring the right people, you're going to have an amazing time. Unfortunately, it's going to cost you much, much more than you're used to paying for Korean food and karaoke, and you've gotta decide if that's worth it for you. 
_____________

*Each room comes equipped with a tambourine (and a disco ball). Take advantage.

Insa is a super cool, trendy but homey kind of place. The bartenders are so friendly and warm, happy to recommend their favorites and really take care of you! The food at Insa is really great as well. They serve whiskey, wine, beer and have private karaoke rooms for large groups. Grab a bunch of friends for food, drinks and karaoke! A+ for the new digs in Park Slope.

I've been here four times now and it has always been a fantastic meal and experience.  The house cocktails are outstanding.  I've had the Jade Emperor and tried their special Soju Bloody Mary for brunch.  I've had the beef brisket on the table grill twice, the Bi Bim Bap, and recently had the fried chicken, which was fantastic.  The banchan are always fresh and delicious and you never get exactly the same things twice, which is always a nice surprise. Also recommended are the kimchi dumplings.  Service is super-friendly and efficient, and they are one of the new wave of restaurants that pay their waiters a living wage to you don't have to tip.  I also got a group together for a karaoke night back in January and it was a big success.  Love this place.

Definitely not worth the prices. The taste isn't up to par either. You're paying for the atmosphere and the convenience of not having to drive to ktown. The dumpings were bland. The steak tartar was one note only. Sesame oil! And the meats were under seasoned. I won't be going back here. Don't forget small portions.

Basically amazing. I have been wanting to go here for a while and it couldn't have been better. The service was impeccable, the food was really fucking good, and the atmosphere was great too. Fresh good and tasty and happy. I will be back.

I love The Good Fork and knew this place would be great, and it is! Lovely space, great meats, and the karaoke rooms are awesome. I've been there with adults and loved it but also brought two kids around 6pm and they had so much fun cooking and then singing with their very drunk auntie. Great staff. Highly recommend!

We had our wedding at a venue across the street, and when our time was up there we spontaneously headed across the street to Insa. We got a large Karaoke room, and although it was late, and a large rowdy group, everyone at Insa was so accommodating and gracious. They really made our night and our wedding. Can't thank them enough!

Bad service, rude waitress and other emoyees. Could not accomodate a party of 12, after spending over 500 bucks on a private room, drinks and food!! I was told to put my nanme down on the wait list as soon as I come in and they would accommodate us after our karaoke  time was over. So 2 hours in advance I placed my name and was told they would  try their best!! Their best was, sorry your party of 12 will have to wait almost 45 mins for a table.  With children we were told to wait at the bar!! And all our food was half packed for us and the other half we were told to.pack ourselves and get out!! After being so rude and us complaining and half of our party walking out; they then tried to accommodate us. By then i had to take care of my angry guests , so we walked out. I don't recommend this place to anyone. Took our money and went to  another restaurant instead!!

Paid $45 for 2 soups (takeout) and got home to find that they filled the containers about two-thirds of the way. 1 piece of meat in the Suhlung tang. Yukweh jang tasted like sesame oil jang. No side dishes (ban-chan). I thought Moim was bad. This is even worst. Never again. 

This is the saddest excuse for a Korean restaurant I've EVER seen (and I've lived in San Francisco). The food isn't bad, but this kind of hipster douchebaggery is just insulting. If you're dying for Korean food, keep dying all the way to the city, Queens or Fort Lee.

My bf and I went around 9:30 and the place was very busy. We saddled up at the bar which also served a full menu, so it was a great option. They offer a handful of lesser known breweries' beers on draft and have the classic korean imports bottled- Hite, OB. They also have signature cocktails, an extensive wine list, sake, and shoju, if beer is not your thing.

We ordered the kimchi and mung bean pancake, fried chicken (half order) and the spicy  squid with udon noodles. The fried chicken and the squid  was exceptional. The fried chicken was completely balanced of sweet, spicy and salty with perfectly crispy skin and the half portion was generous.The squid was also absolutely delicious, tender and not chewy in the slightest.

This place is definitely a "scene" for the moment but the food and fun ambiance makes it worth the trip.
While the food was decent, the experience left a lot to be desired. In fact, the only thing more mediocre than their service is their ability to split checks

Sorry but the food is simply not authentic Korean. Great service and extremely attentive staff. They treated the Korean culture very well and you can order in Korean and their understanding was seamless. But the lack of authenticity was overbearing. 

Don't order stews or soups as they are more Brooklyn fusion than Korean, maybe that's why it's so expensive. The Karaoke bars are certainly a plus but the creative behind the food was too overreaching. Keep it simple and I might come back.

What a cool space with a great concept-Koren BBQ and Karaoke all in one place-it screams out great birthday spot. I came here with a few friends and there was a little wait for a Friday night even though we called ahead. The bring a whole bunch of light mostly if not all veggie salad snacks to start out with, but I had no idea what anything was because the waiter went through everything so fast and I couldn't be sure he was speaking english. The kimchee fried rice was yummy with some pieces of pork belly that made it salty, delicious and savory. We ordered the steak which was great but really just 3 small and very thin pieces, especially for the price. I had a cool green (green tea?) cocktail. The only problem is that everything is overpriced here. Unfortunately they have the market on this cuisine in this neighborhood, so I guess that's how they get away with it!

Went to Insa with my staff and had the best time ever! The food was great, drinks were really yummy, and the service was seamless. We enjoyed two hours of Karaoke post-feast, and i can't remember having so much fun in the past years! I cannot wait to go back again to eat, drink and be merry! Fun! Fun! Fun!

I have been here easily a half dozen times since it opened and I love it. The food is fantastic--particularly the seafood pancake, which is my favorite thing on the menu--and the wait staff is lovely and courteous. The bar is a lot of fun with interesting twists on traditional cocktails, including some unique drinks I've never had before. And then, when you're ready, on to Karaoke in the private rooms in back! It's one-stop shopping for your Saturday night. Or Tuesday. Or Thursday. I can't wait to go back.

3.5 stars. 

Ate and drank at the bar. Absolutely packed to the brim on a Saturday night.

Big props for the fact that they did away with optional tipping, instead pricing their menu such that they can pay their workers a living wage + benefits. Considering that, the prices weren't too bad!

Food was pretty good but nothing too special. I'm probably not going to go out of my way to come back for it, but I'd come back if I was in a group that wanted to eat here. 

Also good: They take reservations! Especially good for groups. 

The cocktails looked good on paper but tasted pretty gross, tbh. Whatever you do, don't get the Dragon King -- it tastes like weird mouthwash. Pick a beer, which goes better with Korean food anyway.

Will have to come back to try out the karaoke rooms, though! There aren't many karaoke rooms in this part of Brooklyn, so Insa's filling a real gap there.

I did enjoy this place yes I did. Rating it higher than its Yelp average and I stand by that.

I was only here for dinner not for karaoke, and here's what the boy and I got:

The Blood sausage - what?! In a Korean restaurant? Yes. And it tastes impressively Asian. I really enjoyed it, they had a good mouth feel, especially cause they were stuffed with lots of little (I want to say, vermicelli?) glass noodles. Also I love blood (not in a murdery kind of way just in a classy boudin noir lover kind of way).

The beef short rib Galbi bbq - yummmmmmmmmm meeeeeaaaaaat.
You can decide if you want them to cook it or if you want to, but we chose to do it ourselves cause we like our meats rarer than the average person. Hence:

The beef tartare - what an interesting dish. Not super Korean tasting with its caper and Asian pear mixed in, but I did enjoy it and the seaweed chip it came with.

The rice cakes - have a well deserved reputation you should obviously just get it cause everyone here tells you to its awesome.

I think that's it. + ban chan obvs. They were really good to us about refilling them I don't know what other people are talking about. They were fine nothing super exciting.

We also got to avua Mai Tais which were tres delicious.

very interesting ambience and serving style with long tables and dividers to divide parties. It's a big open room with lots of space and I love it, but if you want cozy and ambience, there's a lounge bar area that you can get comfy in.

I like it. It's in the middle of nowhere so I probably won't be back, but I like it.

I made a reservation for dinner + karaoke two months in advance. I don't normally buy into the hype of new restaurants with long waitlists, but I was pretty interested in this place. A Korean restaurant with karaoke in super hip Brooklyn? I'd happily make the trek down here to eat with friends who live in the neighborhood, rather than constantly meeting in the middle in Manhattan K-town.

But that's not going to happen, because this whole experience was a huge disappointment. The food is actually excellent (despite the portion size being small), but the entire experience was colored by poor management of the restaurant.

I eat a lot of Korean food. I know what things are called. The menu items are written in romanized Korean. So why was it so hard to order things by their Korean name? Despite not being Korean herself, I was expecting that our waitress would understand the names of Korean dishes we wanted to order, because she works at a Korean restaurant. The only way we managed to order anything was by reading the English description underneath. Why would you not train your waitstaff to understand the Korean names of dishes? Oh, because the ownership is not actually expecting Korean people or people who eat Korean food on the regular to show up. Gotcha. That's why you opened a restaurant up in Hip Brooklyn.

We ordered samgyupsal, and the sesame oil with the rock salt was noticeably missing. When we inquired about it, the man who stepped in to grill our meat for us told us there was salt in one of the other sauces. Nope. That's not what you eat with samgyupsal. It would have been perfectly reasonable for him to say, "Oh, I can bring you some of that, but you should try it with this other sauce, which we prepared specially for the pork belly." I'm interested in trying new things when they've been thoughtfully put together, but that wasn't the case here. The sesame oil with rock salt was only available upon request. 

No refills on banchan. The waitstaff was bewildered when we asked, we had to ask repeatedly, and they came back with banchan for one side of the table, and an entire plate of lettuce long after we'd finished grilling the meat. The waitstaff were not trained that banchan is supposed to be refilled upon request.

I don't need to eat Korean food served by Koreans. However, this was an incredibly expensive dinner served by staff with no understanding of Korean cultural norms. Ganso, which is also in Brooklyn, proves that this does not have to be the case! Ganso serves Japanese food, doesn't have Japanese waitstaff, and still respects the culture they are presenting. It comes down to training your servers to represent the culture you are presenting to your customers, which the owners appeared to not spend time doing.

The transition between dinner and karaoke was really awkward. The people serving us in the restaurant ignored us after we paid our bill, and there wasn't any communication about when our karaoke room would be ready. We figured that we should wait in the bar for our room to be available, again, with no one communicating anything to us. 

At the time of our karaoke reservation, I approached the hostess again, mentioned our karaoke reservation, and she said there was still a group in there, and that needed to get them to pay, and then clean the room for us. When the big group finally left fifteen minutes later, I again approached the podium, and she said that they just left, and that they needed to get the room in order. Ten minutes later, she saw me approaching, and left the podium in advance. I waited a few minutes, and a different host appeared, and the original hostess did not return. I then had to explain the situation to him again, and he went to go talk to her. We finally got into the room 30 minutes after our reservation, were promised by the hostess that we'd get our original 2 hour reserved time slot, only to be approached an hour and thirty minutes after we'd begun, to tell us that our reservation was coming to an end, and we needed to start packing up and leaving. Again, we had to explain to one of the employees exactly what happened, and it took about five minutes of explanation to get everything sorted (five minutes I could have been singing Alanis Morissette, FYI). 

Look Insa, if you're going to charge really high prices, you'd better have your shit together. There was literally nothing that we did here that we couldn't have done in K-town with less stress and frustration, and for less money. It's a shame that the whole operation is so poorly managed, because the food is actually quite good! There is nothing about this business that is worth the two month reservation in advance. If you want the real Korean food/karaoke experience, there are plenty of places that fit the bill in K-Town or Flushing. Don't waste your hard earned dollars here.

Hands-down the best new restaurant I've experienced in Park Slope/Gowanus in years.

Dishes were delicious and well thought out - very traditional Korean influences with a playful modern twist.  We got the yuk hwe (perfection!) and the pork belly, which was rich and satisfying and balanced well with the most addictive kimchi.  The rice cakes were a revelation though - perfectly crispy on the outside, served with yummy fish cakes, veggies, and an intense tomato sauce.  Kind of mind-blowing.

Service was great - friendly, knowledgeable, and attentive.

And the space is beautiful - spacious with clean rounded lines, like being in the hull of a ship, with a shiny open kitchen.  And the lighted cherry tree in the bar is a magical touch!

Perfect spot for a date, family dinner, or just drinks at the bar.  Oh and they have karaoke too!   Will be making this a regular weekend spot for sure! :)

This is one of the best new restaurants in Gowanus. Little Neck now moves to second. Food was great, from the bar snacks to the personal tabletop bbq.  Phew, I no longer need to trek into midtown. Of course, it's Gowanus so watch out for extra long facial hair on the hipsters brining Williamsburg to South Brooklyn.

T.H. and I have been here twice in the past month or so, once during a weekday and once during a weekend. 

The first time we went, we were pleasantly surprised by the quality of the food and general offerings of the menu. As a small group of 4 people, we ordered the ttoekboki (fried rice cakes and vegetables in gochujjang), haemul pajeon (seafood pancake) for appetizers, and ordered three orders of yangyum kalbi. As a Korean myself, I'll admit that the food was well executed and tasted great. 

The second time, we went as a group for a dinner party of 10 followed by karaoke which is also offered here. This is kind of where things fell apart a little. So, we ordered several for the table dishes and only three orders of barbeque as my friends were more entertained by the variety of items than just meat. Part way through splitting and eating these items (the tteokboki again, haemul pajeon, the yukhwe (beef tartare), and fried chicken) the barbeque came out and the bonchon stopped. As a large party, we quickly ate the bonchon which is normally not only continuous in Korean restaurants but also replaced before you even notice. While normally asking for more does not bother me, we had to request a refill on our bonchon 4 times before another set of bonchon came out and only for one side of our table. Okay, so bonchon is hard to get on refills. 

So the other part that I was a little sad about was that one order of kalbi barely fills you up. We had problems with this the first time we went, even going so far as to ordering 3 orders despite having several dishes to share for only four people. The barbeque on the weekend was much of the same. We ordered a normal yangyum kalbi (marinated short rib), ssamgyupssal (pork belly), and octupus and squid. Each order, while delicious, was quite small.

Okay, so we've covered that I liked the food, but the portions were a little small and that the bonchon which is normally endless in Korean restaurants was hard to come by. Verdict on the restaurant? Good food, but for the price and normal amenities that I get at other Korean restaurants, I'll pass.

Karaoke!
So my friend A.P. had reserved a 2 hour block a month or more in advance. What was super disappointing about it all was we got into our room 30 minutes late because the previous group took a while to leave and then they tried to kick us out at the 1.5 hour mark because they said we "showed up late." Now considering we ate at the restaurant beforehand and that we were waiting in their bar area since 9:15 PM, I don't think we could have showed up late for a 10PM reservation. After a bit of arguing, they eventually let us stay in the room to finish our two-hour reservation but I find the whole rigmarole rather tedious for some place advertised as a Korean restaurant and karaoke bar. Fun experience with karaoke? Yeah, but mostly because karaoke is about the people you go with.

Oh boy. Where to begin?

- THE FOOD: Let's get this out of the way, it's great. We really enjoyed the ddeokbokki (rice cake) which was FRIED so it was crispy outside, soft inside. Could have done more sauce though, but I'm sort of gross when it comes to sauce. BBQ squid was tender and delicious also.

- THE PRICE: Menu prices are high, plus there is 20% service charge mandatory on all checks. I find this disingenuous, and if there's already sticker shock you might as well turn it up all the way and make it so that the price you see in the menu is literally what you pay out the door. That is a level of honesty that I would find refreshing in NYC. 9 of us paid $35-40 pp and no one was full.

- TIKI DRINKS: Was truly excited by the prospect of Korean food and Tiki drinks. I love Tiki drinks, both taste and presentation, but here in NYC it's hard to find quality stuff (good fruit juices, not oversweetened, good presentation.) We ordered a Scorpion Bowl, it literally came in a melamine noodle bowl that I eat my breakfast out of, with a melamine ladle, large wedges of ice and some Chinese restaurant style orange slices. It was sickly sweet and so full of cinnamon, it was like cough syrup. $40. We choked it down as we could not bear the idea of wasting our investment.

- WHITEWASHED AND IGNORANT SERVICE: I could not request any dish by its Korean name. I had to read the English description below each item to the Caucasian waitress. BTW, Romanized dish names are printed on the menu, so I expected the server to be on the level. Ordered pork belly BBQ, had to request the sesame oil - salt dip after describing it to non-Korean grill master (who also chastised me for slightly burning some of the last order of BBQ.) I think if you are serving Korean food, no matter who you are, you should know the dishes and what they go with. I felt a large cultural ignorance from the waitstaff here. There was also NO front of house person who appeared to be Asian except the hapa hostess. I am not saying you need one, but the complete absence of any was strange to me.

- SIDE DISHES: They weren't bad. The problem was refilling them. This is a known quantity in any other Korean restaurant in the world. I believe they just simply didn't understand what we wanted. In the end, they just brought us a single plate of kimchi and a pile of lettuce, long after we had finished our BBQ dishes, so totally useless. I think this wasn't malicious; they simply didn't understand what was meant by refilling side dishes. Again, cultural ignorance.

- DASHED PROMISES: Our plan was simple. Dinner at 8pm, transition to Karaoke at 10pm, until midnight. Obviously, dinner would not take precisely 2 hours so we expected to wait. But we waited until 10:30pm as they were not able to boot the last party out of the room in time. Were promised by the hostess that we would get 2 hours of time starting at 10:30p. Then, at 11:50p, server enters (no knocking, just comes in) and presents the bill, saying they need the room at midnight and that we started at 10pm, "right?" Having been fed up by all the other things, we unload on her; we were not proud of this but were so angry from before. Ultimately, host gets involved, says we are good till 12:30. A big distraction. At 12:15, we begin draining our playlist in preparation for leaving, by 12:25 they are standing outside staring at us. Our goal was to have empty playlist and pack up at 12:30 sharp, but in the end they still managed to steal some time away from us.

And why is it OK for the group occupying the room before us to exceed by 30 mins, but not for us to begin leaving the room exactly on schedule instead of 5, 10 min before? The double standard made my blood boil.

- NOBODY HOME: Many private karaoke rooms have a phone or button that can be used to request service. The standard of service I expect from even trashy places (e.g. Japas 55) is that the phone will be picked up or a waiter will come to the door to help you out within 30 seconds to 1 minute. I am not sure exactly how long I waited, but someone definitely sang a whole song -- not sure of the length. Wasn't very happy with that.

- BEER MISADVENTURES: A small glimmer of light. I broke a beer glass attempting to remove it from a stack (that I created.) Glass shards fell into our pitcher, they refilled and brought back plastic cups for all and did not charge us for the glass'd pitcher. That was very nice of them.

If it's not totally clear, I don't think I'd ever come back here. I really like the food which is why it gets 2 stars instead of 1. There is something of value here, but something drastic needs to change with the service before I can think about returning. They first and foremost need to understand the culture they are presenting. Secondly, they just need to learn how to operate a private room karaoke joint. That was some strictly amateur shit.

Sigh. Just go to 32nd St instead of wasting your time here.

Me and my friend Nadia Z. arrived at the restaurant early than our other friend Jenn F. We walked inside the restaurant and the hostess informed that dinner starts at 5:30pm and was asked to wait in the bar area. Later on as we were waiting, the hostess was mumbling something that I have no clue what exactly she said but Jenn F. went over to the podium and told her our name. Okay we were the second people that came into the restaurant and was seated almost last as the hostess never even bother to take down our name...ugh! When we finally get a table, the server was going to put us on a table meant for 8 where there were plenty of emptied 4 seaters back the wall so I demand one for us which we did get one. 

BBQ: 
Samgyeopsal (Thick Sliced Pork Belly) $28 - the description clearly stated THICK sliced pork belly but hell no it was thin like BACON and I love the fatty part of the pork belly. I definitely didn't taste it and that was such a disappointment =(

Yangnyum Gaibl (Marinated Beef Short Ribs) $35 - DAMN this was quite expensive and it isn't Wagyu Beef

Haemul Pajeon (Seafood & Scallion Pancake) $17 - this was tasty like every other Korean style pancake

Oh yea don't forget as Jenn F. mentioned 20% Admin Fee is added to the bill and no need to tip that's how they get their customers. 

Crossed this off my list and never returning! As I left half full and disappointment!
Fabulous place for a party!  I rented the large karaoke room -- food, service, karaoke, and drinks were all great!

I have to give them five stars to offset all of the one to two star reviews! I was expecting a mediocre experience based on these low reviews but my coworkers and I (8 of us total) just visited Insa last night for dinner and karaoke and had a great time. Service was fantastic. Really friendly servers. And everything came out timely. Food was good. Portions are smaller than in ktown and you don't get as many banchan but then again, you're not in ktown. We reserved their small karaoke room, which is $60 per hour, for 6 pm but when we got there, we decided to eat first and they didn't give us any trouble for not going into the room until about 8 pm. Would definitely visit again!

Oh yelp. I should have listened to you and not to Pete Wells.

Fine. Meh. Ho-hum. 

Is that really what you want to say about the new, hotly anticipated Korean bbq in your neighborhood? Just a sad disappointment, mainly due to an utter lack of reality in portions for price. 

I'm fine with spending $30 for galbi, provided that it ends up being a heaping pile of glistening, chewy, sweet lusciousness. Remember steak-ums? That's what we got: 5 pieces of paper thin mystery meat tended by otherwise excellent waitstaff that burnt to a dry jerky like crisp by the time it was pulled from the grill.  Too thin and barely enough for us each to have more than a tiny bite. 

The non-grilled pork belly dish was far more generous, EXCEPT for the sauce. This was a theme of the night...the grill squid and octopus seafood dish was served with about a tablespoon of sauce to split amongst 4 people. Why? Why not give enough to go around? If the protein is meant to serve a group where at least 2 of the 4 folks are fasting, why not at least give us enough sauce to make our minuscule bite exciting? In essence, it was just a piece of grilled squid, which again, given the quantity, we felt cheated having ordered.

The banchan was much glorified in a few reviews and well, again, soooo disappointing.  Nothing unique, but also nothing that felt particularly palate-pleasing or enlivening. I want my banchan to be a cozy welcome to a meal that promises nuanced, interesting flavors and dazzling piles of protein inviting you to dig in. 

This was not our experience at Insa. Sigh. Guess we'll need to continue to schelp to Koreatown or Flushing to get our K-BBQ fix.

My experience was the opposite of most other reviewers. I found the service to be great, attentive without feeling overbearing. I did not have similar warm feelings for the food. 

We shared four dishes at the table. The non-BBQ dishes were OK. The BBQ dishes left a lot to be desired. The portions were very small and the waited who was nice enough to cook did a good job with the seafood but the meat was way over. I can't really blame him though. The four pieces were so tiny anything longer than 10 seconds on the grill would overcook it. 

I think the best way to describe how the meal was is that the day after our meal my wife made me go to the butcher to buy meat to make Korean at home that night.
Nice and cool place but look like hall ! Food are good and yummy ! Price are ok :)  kimchi and pork soup are so yummy ! Like it

Don't go here. The service we got was so bad I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone.  Go to Koreatown in Manhattan. It will be worth it.  We went their for our anniversary.  First, they misquoted our time.  We got there at 9:00 and said we would eat by 10:30.  We didn't sit until 11:00 and we didn't get an apology or anything else.  We sat down and our server spoke to us once, took the order, then spoke to us one more time asking if I wanted another drink.  The appetizers were fine but she came up and was very unfriendly when preparing the food at the table.  We were then asked to finish cooking it ourselves.  My girlfriend and I were disappointed to say the least.   We were never asked for dessert and they seemed to be just rushing us out.  20% tip is included which was outrageous given our service.  

There should be a zero star option for places like this.  We will never be back.  

The food was nothing special. 

PS: The drinks were mediocre at best.

Went here  with a few friends for dinner before going to their large karaoke room that we had reserved. The atmosphere of the place was good, very open with picnic table style seating. They also, had a nice bar area to wait for our table to be ready.

We ordered some pretty standard Korean dishes with each having some varying levels of quality to them:
Banchan - Good variety of dishes came up with solid flavor
Haemul PaJeon - Very good, crispy, and good amount of seafood in the pancake
Galbi - Lacking in the flavors that you expect from galbi and oddly on the saltier side
Samgyupsal - Thick cut and good
ChadolBaeGi - Tasty good quality meat, nicely thin cut
YookGaeJang - Overall good but a bit under flavored to what I'm used to
KimchiJiGae - Pretty good, nothing incredibly special

Overall, I thought the food could be improved to compete with what you can get to easily in Manhattan or Queens. I was hoping that there would finally be a place in Brooklyn for Korean food and BBQ that could keep me from heading to K-Town or Queens but unfortunately I wasn't too excited. Maybe I will give it another try to see if things have gotten a bit better.

In fairness to the kitchen, the food here is excellent. 
But the service is bad.
We arrived on time for our reserved table, just in time to hear the hostess telling someone else the name of the party for which they were holding a table. This may seem nit-picky, but at a certain price point, it's reasonable to expect actual professional service, not hipster, slacker, I'd rather not be here service.
Meanwhile, the table the hostess had just told other people she was holding for us was two feet away and we wanted to sit at it. The hostess told us we could wait in the bar area. The bar area was crowded and, since we had already reserved this table and were going to be patronizing this restaurant with six of our friends, it should be our prerogative whether to sit down, not the hostess's to dictate. I did not want to get into an argument, but we had one of those millisecond moments of non-verbal exchange where she got that I found her refusal to seat us frustrating and, rather than recognize that maybe her job is to assuage that frustration, she countered with the arrogance that I was making problems by simply disagreeing with her choice of where I should stand. 
We had a good time, and again the food was excellent (though what kind of self-respecting Korean place doesn't offer a decent hot sauce?), but I was struck by the contrast between the type of experience they presume to offer and the lack of training they seem to have given to help provide that experience, which gives the place an overall vibe of cynicism and greed. 
Doubt I'd go back, and certainly wouldn't recommend it to friends.

be sure to make a reservation, this place was completely packed.

i've been to many korean restaurants and eaten korean food my entire life so i'm going to review the food only.

we ordered the dolsot bi-bim-bap and the galbi-chim.
the dolsot bi-bim-bap was good - average. the galbi chim was burnt. burnt. i have never had a galbi chim taste worse...! the stewed root veggies were under-done. it was really bad and i was thusly extremely disappointed to have gotten "the best dish on the menu" according to one of the servers. i truly don't understand how they can mess up stewing some meat and root veggies. it was bewildering.

there was absolutely no ban-chan. so no kimchi. oh and the galbi-chim was not served with rice on the side. so yeah, not ideal. 

this place might be hip. but if i want good korean food i will just have to make the trek to Queens or Manhattan. really unfortunate, i was hoping this would replace the excellent korean restaurant Moim in the slope that has closed its doors not too long ago.

Not great. Rude staff. The bartender was just outright mean. Food is meh, service is super slow (though there weren't many people there, even on a Saturday night), and SO expensive for no reason. Also, yeah, included automatic 20% gratuity means they give you bad service and there's nothing you can do. Go to Korea town if you want actually good food and karaoke that's half the price! Don't go here.

Unfortunately, I can't recommend this place. Made a Yelp account just to comment about how bad our experience was here. Food is mediocre, the karaoke rooms are overpriced, and the staff was incredibly rude. Very disappointed because I had heard great things about this place! Our server in the karaoke room was so excellent, but the female bartender was TERRIBLE. Drinks are shockingly overpriced (automatic 20% gratuity...which I 100% support for excellent service! But the service from our bartender was terrible. We were forced to pay for terrible service.) Hopefully, they hire better bartenders, improve the food, and justify the pricing. Overall a pretty negative experience. There are lots of great places in Gowanus....please don't waste your money here!
Terribly disorganized. Delivered wrong food to group party in karaoke room, repeatedly made it impossible to sort or the bill at the end.

Very expensive for what you get: We went here for my friends birthdays today. It was nice food but service from our main server was well... Meh. We had a table booked for 10 however 7 was the final number and they had us cramped on to a table what didn't really work. We had to ask several times for a solution so that we more comfortable. The server that came to the table with the meat however was very sweet and gave us direction on what goes with what ect. Once it was time for Karaoke we were greeted by a nice lady who was short In her tome however explained that is was just her to 5 kareoke rooms each holding 10 to 19 people so I get why she was so busy and not up for chit chat. We all ordered drinks at the beginning of the hour we had in the room and our Drinks came with only 25 mins or 15 mins to spare. I wouldn't rush back but Good place to go for silly and fun expensive night out.

Good ambience with poor taste. 

I was really excited because it was really hard to find a Korean restaurant in Brooklyn. The interior was okay, they tried to give us a hint of Korean design with Brooklynish ambience. However, the overall quality of food was not satisfying. 
Frankly speaking, I may cook better Korean dishes than they do. Their balance within dishes was not that of Korean and the meat had no flavor. 

Furthermore, they preclude 20% tips to your bill after tax. To make it clear, you are going to pay more than 20% from your pretax bill as a mission. 

Service was okay but well, I was not sure if their service was that decent.

The place was so crowded we were told it would be a two-hour wait, but we managed to get a seat in the bar, and could order most everything, except for the BBQ items... The service was attentive, and the food was excellent. We had to order a second round of the Tteokbokki, it was so good. We had some pescatarians in our party, so we didn't order any of the meat dishes.  I'm looking forward to returning to try them, and the bbq.  We were so full by the time a table was free that we didn't bother moving to the main room.

Really solid Korean food - the grilled fish is great, as is the miso stew. The meat is not to my taste (too sweet) but given the choice between this, or schlepping to 32nd St or to Queens as alternatives, this will certainly do fine. I don't know what these negative service comments are about - we've been there twice now and it's been great both times.
Love everything about this place. The bar is great. Drink selection amazing. Food has a great variety and plenty of options. Service was spot on. Haven't seen a place like this in Brooklyn. Big fan.
Food's good but the service sucks.  Don't even try getting a drink at the bar.  Oh and by the way, a 20% gratuity is built into your drink tab so you can't do anything about it.

Four star food, zero stars for service.  20% is automatically added to EVERYTHING, our server was definitely not service oriented. Went last night, a party of 10 people.

Beautiful decor.

I arrived late, the server didn't even acknowledge me, I was not offered a menu, a drink or even a glass of water. I eventually asked the host for the wine list and he courteously got me my drink.  

Karaoke rooms were great, went to the bar for a $13 glass of wine. Was automatically charged $2.60 "service fee" disgusting! Felt totally ripped off.

I am a server myself. And do not usually write reviews, but really feel that if this server is typical of all the servers at this place they will be the death of Insa.
Setting up camp here in one of the karaoke rooms, siphoning Mai Tais/engineering a pully system to retrieve dumplings and kimchi from the kitchen for as long as I can get away with it A++

We went to Insa several weeks ago with a party of seven.  We were a mixture of a native Koreans, Korean-Americans, a Jewish-American from Long Island, an Italian, and two transplanted mid-westerners, ranging in age from late twenties to young sixties.  Not only do we all get along, we all agreed that the food at Insa is amazing!  The ingredients are fresh and tasty, and the dishes are creatively prepared and presented.  Particularly good were the  (beef tatar) and grilled branzino.  We definitely will return!

This is so awful I'm not even waiting to leave Insa to write this. 

Have you ever watched a snail cross the street? Service is even slower.
They'll rush you though, so hurry up and cook that meat they haven't brought you yet.
We had to cancel part of order because "we need the table."


13 minutes. 
That's how long it takes to receive a scotch neat. You know, a drink that is a quick pour of one thing in a glass. Someone else at my table waited longer. My table isn't half a mile from the bar.

Booked a karaoke room. Getting alcohol was a 45 minute wait. We ordered bottles and a pitcher. Over an hour later, pitcher still isn't here. 

Btw: kbbq is a communal dining experience but they only take 4 cards per table and aren't totally sure where the nearest atm is. Make sure y'all have venmo I guess? 

Where is my negative star option?

Huge space, delicious food and karaoke rooms.

Pros tips: 
-This KBBQ will NOT leave you smelling like a greasy grill! Kudos to whomever designed the ventilation at Insa.
-They have nut-milk cocktails ...YEAHYUH!
-Two words: Kara-okay! The rooms are discreetly connected to the restaurant. And the song list is pretty current!

I'm not a Korean BBQ connoisseur, but some food tips:
-Grilled fatty pork is tasty
-Grilled seafood is a bit tasteless, but a great option if you don't want fatty meats
-Seafood pancake could have been better 
-Skip the steamed dumplings, opt for fried

Tip is included under "Admin Fee" on the bill.

$60 an hour (per room) for karaoke.

Great service in the restaurant and karaoke rooms!

I haven't been on Yelp in a long time because my grandson moved to Connecticut last year and I haven't been able to go out to these great new places. But now he's back because he broke up with his girlfriend which is fine with me. So we went for Korean food! How exotic! My father was in the Korean War and if he was alive he wouldn't like this so much. But it was so very good. Interestingly it is in Gowanus. When I was a girl we we wouldn't cross the canal to this area because all the workman would whistle at us and chase us down the street. But this place was fantastic. The chicken wings were out of this world and not the kind that you get when you go to a friends party. And strangely enough they don't allow tipping. Can you get that? It's crazy. I was concerned because they bartender was a young lady (but plenty of young ladies are bartenders now, I know). But she said she liked it because she always knew how much money she'd make. It's funny. Although she hand't heard of a whiskey sour, but I showed her. I hope I can go here again with my grandson soon.

I give it 4.5 thumbs up out of a scale of 5 thumbs.

My group of 4 went to Insa for dinner last Sat and waited literally 3 hours to get seated. Was it worth it? Not exactly. The food was good: Stonebowl Bimbim Bap is probably the best I have ever had, other items we ordered (brisket bbq, jap chae) were okay but not worth the 3-hour wait. Why the 4 stars? Well, the General Manager was more than accommodating. Due to the unexpected long-wait, she made sure we were well taken care off and gave us a very nice discount on our meal. I definitely appreciate this gesture and will certainly come back on a non-weekend night so we can enjoy a meal without the long wait

What Park Slope/Gowanus needed was good Korean barbeque. Add on karaoke and I am sure people are lining up around the block to try this place out. I have to admit: I am a sucker for Korean barbeque and soju. Typically, we would have to go to K-town in Manhattan or Queens to get some good Korean food. 

I had high hopes that Insa would be the calling for Brooklyn. Although Insa did satisfy the need for Korean barbeque, it did not satiate my cravings. Insa had the fundamental Korean dishes that we wanted - japchae, bimbimbop, mandoo dumplings, spicy rice cakes, various meats/seafood to grill on. The food was good but I would say some of these dishes have a modern take on the traditional Korean foods (e.g., Rice cakes had a drizzle of hot sauce and was crunchy). 

As Insa is still new, several kinks that they could work on:
(1) Wait time - For a party of 6, we were told that it would take 1.5 - 2 hours. After 2.25 hours and not hearing from the restaurant, we went back to check on our status. After waiting a bit more, they were finally able to get us a table. 
(2) Air ventilation - The restaurant was smoky mostly due to poor air ventilation as there are no air vents above the grills. 
(3) Service - We did not know who our server was.  There were several servers that delivered food or helped out at our table. This resulted in lack of accountability as we would ask servers for extra lettuce, hot sauce, or another drink and nothing would be delivered. 

We didn't check out the karaoke because they were booked out for the night. For future reference, book the room well in advance.

What a great new addition to Brooklyn! I ate here with my dad visiting from out of town and we had an excellent meal and a great time. The dining room is spacious and warm- and we loved the looks of the cozy bar. I'm used to trekking to Ktown for bbq and wasn't sure how this would stack up, but the food was amazing. 
Ban chan was out of this world and the pork belly prepared at our table was fantastic. Also loved the fried dumpling app! The service was also warm and friendly- when a server didn't know the answer to one of my questions she said so and came right back with what I needed to know. I'll be back with soon my husband to try out more of the menu.
Thank you Insa for coming to Brooklyn!

$13 for a tequila well shot?? Yeah you will not have a returning customer. Sorry!
You are super expensive!
Also, if you charge an administration fee... How about you explain what it is. That's SUPER sneaky!!!

Korean BBQ in Brooklyn? Yeah buddy. 

Another sign of change and gentrification in the area.

Went here for dinner on a Saturday night with a group of 6. The wait was 2 hours, so went to a few bars in the area to kill time. The wait is not their fault at all, it's actually a sign that people are over going to Flushing Queens for KBBQ, about 45 -60 mins aways. 

We had the following items:

Starters
Gogi Mandu - steamed dumplings
Haemul Pajeon - Seafood & Scallion Pancake
Tteokbokki - Spicy Rice Cakes, Fish Cakes, Soft Boiled Egg
Bibimbap - Vegetables over Rice, Gochujang Sauce, Fried Egg 

Meats/BBQ
Yangnyeom Galbi -Marinated Beef Short Ribs
Chadolbaegi - Thinly Sliced Beef Brisket
Ojingeo & Nakji - Cuttlefish & Octopus

My Drink
Tiger's Whisker (Blanco Tequila, Ssamjang Agave, Green Salt, Citrus)

All of the food was great quality and in good size portions. My favorites were the dumplings, short rib, and brisket. The drink I had was very creative and delicious.

The service was fast and friendly. You can BBQ yourself or they can do it for you.

They also have a few karaoke rooms in the back and very modern wood work decor inside. I just wish the ventilation was a bit better, super smoky inside. 

Final Verdict -  great stuff if you don't want to go to the Asian areas for KBBQ, as for me, I don't mind making the trip out to Flushing or other areas. So after this fun outing, I will still be going to the Asian areas for my next KBB fix.

Delicious Secret
Insa Korean Restaurant is a delicious three-week old secret on an industrial side street. Service is excellent and attentive. The well-ventilated space is a welcome alternative to the usual barbecue smoke-filled rooms. Copious vegetable banchan come with the main dishes and the barbecues are large enough to share. Tender galbi, excellent sweet potato noodles and tasty seafood or kimchee pancakes are all offered in generous portions. Thanks to the owners for bringing authentic and delicious Korean food to the neighborhood!

Came here for dinner and also had some drinks/food in the bar area. Everything was good, atmosphere was very cool. Can't speak to the authenticity as others may have but it didn't seem dissimilar to any Ktown BBQ places food-wise. Pretty expensive for the cuisine type and especially for the location. 

Mandatory 20% fee, independent of group size, not even indicated as "gratuity". It was off putting, especially since it is included regardless of whether you're at the bar, at a table being served, at a BBQ table and having a waiter cook your food on a grill, etc, ie at a place where there are clear distinctions in levels of service. If the fee is intended to support the wages of the staff, just bake the cost into higher prices.

I would like to give them 10 stars,  The fried chicken, the pork belly the short rib...
The presentation was awesome, the service SONJIA, beyond and above.  This is a diamond.  Everyone should go here.

Ladies. Gentlemen. Insa is fabulous. Here's my breakdown:

Ambience/Design (5 stars): This is one of the most beautifully designed and curated restaurants I've ever had the pleasure of experiencing. It's tough for a place to be both refined and warm/inviting, but Insa definitely pulls that off. 

Drinks (5 stars): Despite the somewhat caricature-y Asian names, the cocktails are subtle, delicious, and interesting. I would highly recommend the K-Town Old Fashioned, Silk Punch, and Dragon King. Oh, and they have their soju distilled in Brooklyn - that stuff is delightful.

Service (3.5 stars): Service could use work, but it's been improving with every visit. At first, it seemed as though the wait staff weren't able to discern between certain dishes while ordering. Maybe it's just me, but I like be a tad understanding re: service at a brand new restaurant. I'd love to bring my service rating to a 5, and I'm confident Insa will make that happen soon enough. 

Karaoke (1,000 stars): I am a Karaoke aficionado. I used to prefer stage karaoke because a lot of the room-based karaoke places in K-town were a little grimy and smelly despite the high cost. But, I am now a changed woman. The karaoke systems themselves are stellar - the backing tracks are real, and the reverb on the mics makes everyone sound like a superstar diva. The themes are fun, the sound is great, and the rooms are clean and perfect. 

Food (4.5 stars): I'm a little confused by the content of some of the negative reviews, here. Of course taste and authenticity are subjective, but quality/freshness is certainly not. I should preface by saying that I am Korean (a pretty "bad" one though, whatever that means), and have consumed a great deal of the food of my people throughout my life. This doesn't make me an expert, but I know what I like, and I know when food is fresh and of high-quality. Here are my ratings of the dishes I've had, so far:

Gogi Mandu (5 stars) - This meat dumpling was fried to perfection, seasoned wonderfully, and could not have been tastier.

Yache Mandu (5 stars) - The vegetarian version of their Mandu is equally delightful. It has mixed vegetables and a little bit of kimchi. I would recommend getting this fried.

Insa Fried Chicken (3.5 stars) - I've had the fried chicken a couple of times now, and each time it's been a bit salty. However, the actual chicken is fried beautifully with a crispy outside and an incredibly tender and moist inside. 

Yuk Hwe (5 stars) - I had never had this Korean beef tartare before coming to Insa, so I don't really have a frame of reference. But this is freaking delicious, everyone. So beefy, with little bits of Asian pear to offset the meatiness. I've had this all three times I've been to Insa. Ugh. 

Galbi (4 stars) - This is actually the most delicious galbi I've ever had, but, I gave it four stars instead of five because of the price. But for special occasions, I think it's totally worth it.

Chadolbaegi (4 stars) - I never had Chadolbaegi (thinly sliced brisket) made on the grill before. This is unseasoned, and requires that the beef be of great quality, which it was. Again, the docked star is for the price. 

Beosut Modeum (5 stars) - Oh my goodness. I never knew mushrooms could be so remarkable. With a nice assortment of shrooms thrown on the grill, any fungus fan would be thrilled by the quality and intense flavors from this dish.

Grilled Branzino (5 stars) - BOMB. SO GOOD. Moist, flaky, flavorful. Perfection. Get it. 

Kimchi Jjigae (5 stars) - I'm really into this kimchi stew. We could date. It may be a bit milder than what some are used to (this stew is usually made with overly ripe kimchi, and is therefore often beautifully intense and funky). It has a lovely balance between the tanginess and spiciness from the kimchi, and meatiness from the pork. I will probably order this every time I go to Insa.

Soondubu (5 stars) - This is my favorite silky tofu stew I've ever had. In most restaurants, there is so much fat and oil and red pepper flakes in this dish (not a bad thing, at all). But at Insa, the flavors are more delicate (you can actually taste the seafood in the broth), and the shellfish are perfectly cooked.

Galbijjim (4 stars) - This beef stew is amazing. Perhaps best for a special occasion due to cost.

All in all, Insa make me super happy. I think it's hard to be a different kind of Korean restaurant when everyone's frame of reference is really this singular and uniform style of cooking tasted in K-town. It may be helpful to frame your Insa dining through the lens of Brooklyn's brand (ew, I know, but bear with me), where craft and quality reign supreme. I have nothing against the old style of Korean food (I love it, in fact), but I see nothing wrong with doing something a little different. 

I'm obsessed. And I think you should be obsessed, too.
Amazing food, great ambiance, welcome addition to the neighborhood. Can't wait to go back for karaoke!

After a couple hours at BK Boulders a few doors down, we were pleasantly surprised to see a restaurant open that late on Xmas eve. I'm a fan of Korean BBQ but thought I always had to go to KTown. 

Turns out, I still do. 

The restaurant had been open for a week when we discovered it, and it looks brand new. The blonde wood interiors and bench seating are all quite nice. There is a bar that has a separate entrance which is open when the restaurant is closed between meals. Drinks are good, and the soju from Van Brunt was different, but smooth. 

As for the food, the portions of BBQ were pretty small which was disappointing given how expensive it was. We got three pieces of beef in the Kalbi order. Three! 

The japchae and seafood pancake, tho, were really good sizes. 

Regarding the service, they were pretty adamant about grilling all three whopping pieces of beef at once when we were wanting more to take our time. Our waitress was nice but didn't seem like she wanted to be there. Maybe because it was Xmas eve?

We didn't do karaoke but the restaurant was packed with families for Xmas eve dinner. Overall, I wouldn't go out of my way to return especially if I was starving.

New Korean restaurant in Brooklyn. I was very excited to be a patron since I live here in the summer and Xmas. 
Table BBQ and Karaoke rooms. 
Very amateurish and not anywhere close to the Manhattan or queens counterparts. 
I would love to come more often and support this restaurant as a brooklynite but nowhere close to maturity

This is the first new place in a long time by which we've been so impressed. It's a really nice space, for one, and the communal seating portion is executed well. (Incidentally, the museum-style diorama of the Korean countryside by the door is great for when your kid gets bored mid-meal). 

Drinks and cocktails are reasonably priced. I really enjoyed my sake (a junmai from Hiroshima) which was smooth, but not too sweet. My husband had the Dragon King cocktail (mellow corn whiskey, smokey coconut, orange blossom, branca menta, citrus), which was delicious, also.

For our meal, we chose the scallion and seafood pancakes, vegetable fritters, pork belly BBQ, and the short rib, root vegetable, and chestnut stew. They also brought us a savory egg custard.

The seafood and scallion pancake was hands down the best I've ever had. The seafood inside was generous and so much more fresh than seafood that's usually in pancakes like this. I wanted to keep eating it until I had gorged myself. The vegetable fritters were fried tangles of julienned veggies (sweet potato, maybe, and I'm not sure what else). This wasn't bad at all, and was well seasoned and not greasy, but in retrospect, we didn't need another fried starter having gotten the pancakes, so it was overkill for our table of two adults and one small kid. I'd try something different next time.

The pork belly BBQ was well executed by our server. (This is definitely not a "phone-it-in" service job; these guys are working hard). I wish more vegetables had been included, though. There was just one mushroom, cut into two pieces, and a bit more scallion would have been great. Along with the seafood and scallion pancake, the beef short rib stew was a real standout. The short rib was falling off the bone and the vegetables were perfectly cooked, not mushy. The flavor was rich and perfect, not bland, and not too salty. I usually am not a fan of egg custards (too eggy), but this one was so good I wanted to keep eating it, but didn't have room. It was topped with a few black sesame seeds and some scallion greens. It was the perfect temperature, perfectly silky, and not "eggy" at all. Almost like a dessert, but not at all sweet.

I can't wait to go back here and try tons more stuff. These guys have it figured out. They aren't trying to make too many dishes and they are doing what they have chosen to do very, very well.

Super excited to have Insa in the neighborhood, it's a fantastic addition. The food is amazing - so good we went back a second time opening week. We just couldn't get enough. They are still so new and I know overtime this place will knock it out of the park. 

They could make a few improvements and mainly that revolves around staff. There are so many people working there its a bit chaotic and everyone doesn't seem trained on what they are serving. 

On both visits we had servers who showed no interested in us or explaining the menu. Luckily other staff members come and go so if your waiter isn't great, there's someone else right there to assist you. 

When I mentioned my shellfish allergy to our waiter on our second visit, she acted as if I was totally putting her out - even though on our first visit the Chef/Owner came to our table and told us not to worry about anything in regards to cross contamination. For others suffering from shellfish allergies, ask for the vegetarian kimchi -- no shrimp paste! 

When we asked for our check as our baby was getting a little restless while we finished our meal, they started clearing the table even when we were still holding chopsticks and eating- it made us feel like they wanted to flip the table so quickly and we were being pushed out. It was a little strange and not at all representative of the place or the food. I do wonder if the no tip rule and the admin fee means that the waiters don't have to go out of their way, they know they will get paid regardless. 

I hope overtime these kinks will get worked out -  the staff will be more accommodating and friendly and the food will remain as good as it already is.

It's a beautiful space. The bar alone is worth a visit as it's just lovely. As others have mentioned, the service is uneven and the food is nothing to write home about. The bibimbop was lukewarm and the bowl as well. Not authentic at all. We ordered an appetizer which was delivered to the wrong table. Disappointing experience so it's back to K-town for the real deal.

I had been excited for the opening of Insa for a while, especially since it was being opened by Sohui Kim, but I was hugely disappointed in my experience. If you've ever had actual Korean food you would know that what they're serving at Insa is a white-washed version of what Korean food is supposed to taste like. I tried the bulgogi bibimbap, seafood pancake, and tofu jigae. While the ingredients seem fresh enough, the dishes lacked flavor and spice that you expect to find in this type of food. The seafood pancake had barely any seafood in it and was the worst seafood pancake I've ever gotten. The ambiance was nice enough, and the drinks weren't bad, but the service was ridiculously slow. The slow service could have been due to the fact that it was opening week.

I can't speak to the karaoke since I was only there for dinner. I'm sure this place will be teeming with hipsters, so if you're looking for a crowded place with bad Korean food, please enjoy. I will not be there.

Really disappointing. I wanted to love this place because I loved the idea of having Korean food so close to home!!! I guess if you are looking for a good ambience and good drinks and bad Korean food this place is ok. I  give them 2 stars for ambience and Karaoke. But seriously those of you who rarely had Korean food....please do not think this place is a representation of good Korean food. It is certainly more chic and modern than most Korean place you will go in flushing and K town but the food really sucks!!! There is absolutely no BBQ experience because they did not install the proper ventilation so they try to finish cooking asap and close the hear so you are left eating cold meat throughout. (That is never how it is supposed to be done!!) The price of bbq is as expensive as Ktown but the meat is really low quality. I got a over priced Soon tofu which is a classic Korean tofu soup and they had put doenjang in it. Yuk! which is equivalent to serving a chicken pot pie with marinara sauce in it. I am all for fusion dish and creativity but you have to tell me before I am going to get a non soon tofu. I had sent the food back and they told me that is normally how it is done. Either they hired non Korean chef who has no clue or they are lying! Don't even get me started on service. Everyone was confused and people do not know what anything was or how to pronounce anything. Which is ok because it just opened and they hired non Koreans. But they kept getting our orders wrong and never checked on us which is not a good service anywhere in the world. This place sucks and is overpriced. Brooklyners Do yourselves a favor and Uber to flushing or Ktown for Korean food. I can confidently say I have had better Korean food in manhattan delis than here. You will be saving money and get more authentic yummy Korean food anywhere else but here.

Great ambience and tasty mixed drinks, but if you want a good Korean dinner, I do not suggest this spot. I had the kimchee/vegetable dumplings and they were decent-tasting, but over-priced. The kimchee had little flavor. Additionally, my party and I were guilted when we asked for more banchan (side dishes). The bibimbop was not served in a hot bowl to ensure the crispiness of the rice at the bottom. Sad face. Lastly, the waitstaff was inattentive, sometimes verging on rude. I hope this place improves, as I would love to frequent a close by Korean resto.

Ambiance of restaurant: 4 stars

THANK YOU, INSA!!! I have been desperate for a real Korean restaurant in this part of Brooklyn for more years than I care to note.  The recent explosion of Korean-fusion restaurants nearby has only made this desperation stronger.  And now, finally, someone has done it.  Went there for dinner opening week, and to be sure, I was skeptical going in.  (I've tried every one of the new Korean-ish joints, always let-down, to put it mildly.)  But no! This is real Korean food in a gorgeous, fun, laid-back, pretty-much-perfect space.  So happy.  Here's what I love about Insa:

-It's authentic Korean food.  The owners don't assume that non-Koreans can't handle or wouldn't appreciate real Korean food.  (I've never understood that.  I mean, who has tried good Korean food and NOT liked it??)  They even use real Korean names on the menu.  It shows respect for Korean food, Korean people/culture, AND for the non-Koreans invited to join in eating it!  

-The food is excellent.  While I might have appreciated one or two things that were just slightly more funky or spicy, every single thing we had (and we ordered quite a lot) was delicious.  Obviously great ingredients, cooked/seasoned/prepared really well.  The banchan was all super fresh and delicious (and anyone who knows Korean food knows that's a litmus test right there!); the BBQ (we had kalbi and samgyupsal/pork belly) was delicious -- true, the portions were a little smaller than I would have liked, but I'm happy to pay an extra few bucks for the quality of meat and for saving me a trip to Flushing; the bossam/pork belly was insanely delicious -- the best I've ever had; everything else we had was really good, too, including the haemul pajon/seafood pancake, fried mandu/dumplings, dukboki/spicy rice cakes.  Yum, yum, yum.  

-Service was great.  Seems like it might take a second for the servers to get the hang of Korean BBQ, but you gotta give them that.  They were all super, super friendly and attentive, as was the host.

-Cocktails were yummy.  The bar space is cute, too.

-The whole space is gorgeous.  It's a perfect marriage of traditional Korean BBQ place meets hip Brooklyn joint. 

-The karaoke!!  The karaoke rooms (all private, as in traditional Korean karaoke places) are the nicest I've ever been in.  Cute, themed, and with a great selection of songs.  And the quality of the karaoke was great, too.  No cheesy videos or weird electronic versions of the songs here.  (Anyone else with kids ever had the terrible experience of choosing a pop song only to have a totally inappropriate video come on??  I appreciate not having to worry about that. Ha!)  So fun!!  We just did a little karaoke after dinner. Next time we will go for some karaoke and order some food and drinks in there. 

Writing about it makes me want to go back, like, tomorrow.

Thank you, Insa!!

"What Gowanus really needs is a combination Korean BBQ/karaoke spot," is a thought I'd never had before. Luckily, the minds behind the Good Fork work differently.

There's been a ton of buzz around Insa since it was announced (with a brief experimental residency at Threes Brewing across the street), and I can say it definitely lives up to the hype.

They have two entrances - one to the bar, and one to the main restaurant. The bar is cool, with a few booths, great lighting, and a super cool bartender named Andy. They have decidedly Asian-inspired cocktails that I wouldn't expect to find anywhere else in the area. They use ingredients like matcha tea, jujube, and coconut milk.

Once our table was ready (around 10 minutes on opening week), we walked into the main dining area, which was quite the trip. Assuming this space used to be a garage or warehouse, they really did a number to make it look inviting. High ceilings, skylight, long communal tables, and a giant kitchen off to the side. It really feels like a beer hall, but... y'know, Korean.

Our waitress Sonya was hilarious and made some great recommendations. Between three people, we had:
1) Pork/beef/chive dumplings - they come 7 to an order (weird) and we went with fried. Pretty damn good, especially with the sweet-ish dipping sauce.
2) Japchae - a vegetarian noodle dish with egg. It had two types of noodles and a ton of veggies. Good for something light, but I don't think I could've eaten a whole plate of it.
3) Blood sausage - great if you can stomach it, but probably better for sharing among more people. You can only have so much blood.
4) Cuttlefish and octopus for the grill. Great flavor, but in hindsight, we should've asked for it to be grilled longer for more char.
5) Tteokbokki - spicy rice "cake" with fish cakes and egg. This was probably my favorite dish. Very Korean, with a good balance of spicy and savory.

I'd be remiss if I didn't also mention the karaoke. We didn't sing any songs, but they have two room sizes. The smaller one can fit up to 10 people, and they charge by the hour for the room, rather than by the person by the hour, like many places in the city do. It's $60/hour for the small room and $160 for the large. Not bad if you can get a large group going.

Gowanus is definitely shaping up to be a wonderful area for extracurricular activities, and Insa is a very welcome addition to the neighborhood!
